review_text: The Good: Still like what it used to taste like from what I can remember. Hits the spot every time! The Bad: Adel's is a fierce competitor a few blocks down with a long line. BUT, imho Adel's doesn't really taste as good as the original Halal Guys in terms of flavor and fragrance. The chicken from Adel's is in bigger chunks and some argue is more tender, but the flavor is definitely not close. Also, it's important that it comes with lettuce, tomatoes and a little onion to balance everything out. Finally, You must get both the spicy red and white sauce together to make it all come together! The Ugly: The smell is addictive, so if you walk by, it's hard to resist, even if you've just eaten a nice meal somewhere else. We couldn't resist. Gotta hit the gym hard for the next few days!
Thank you for your excellent review! We are glad to hear you are having such a great experience at The Halal Guys. As always, please feel free to let us know if you have any additional feedback.

This is a NYC staple--but on a Friday or Saturday night, the line gets insanely long. Pro tip from a New Yorker: the cart on 53rd & 7th is the exact same--same owners, same food. People skip it thinking it's not the real one, so there's usually little to no line. Even better, it's right by the Shake Shack seating area, so you can actually sit and enjoy your food. Look for the cart next to the "HOPE" statue.
Thank you for the positive comments about The Halal Guys! We are lucky to have customers like you! If we can ever do anything to make your experience even better, feel free to contact us directly.

I used to grab Halal food like once a week - mainly a chicken over rice bowl - from the various food trucks across the city, but the Halal Guys is definitely the most well known and consistent. I've been a more skeptical of food safety and hygiene so feel a bit better coming here to a place that consistently has a long line and good reputation. The line was a big confusing to figure out with the 5 or so people there the one night I was there. From previous times I've passed, Ive seen the line form in a certain direction and when I went to go to where I thought was the end of the line, I see another group go the other end, and all the other line waiters were facing in the opposite direction that I was expecting so it made me second guess my spot in line. I decided to follow the crowd and join behind the last couple I saw get on line. The staff was still preparing their next batch of food so paused on taking orders for a few min. When they restarted, they announced and motioned to all of us that the line forms "that way". So I was right. Wish they had clearer lines. When we all migrated, the order we were in got jumbled, which was very annoying that grown adults don't know how to wait on line and understand the concept of when a line moves, it's socially expected that you re-order yourselves in the same order you were in. Anyway, it was late at night and I didn't have much energy or patience to argue that out.  The line moves quickly anyway. So minus 1 star for general line management. I got my usual chicken over rice with all veggies and hot and white sauce. Delicious and scarfed down the whole bowl in one sitting in maybe 15 minutes.

There are many halal guys carts and restaurants.  For some reason, this particular location just tastes better!  It's a must stop for us every time we visit New York City.  We ate it twice on this trip!  Extra hot sauces is a must!!! Love their fries too!
Hi Edward, thanks for the 5-star review! We appreciate you taking the time out of your day to rate The Halal Guys.

We pick up two beef and chicken combo meal at $12@ and took them home for dinner. Ended up sharing one and each of us had a full plate of beef, chicken, Spanish rice, salad and pita bread. They were delivered with their own special white sauce.
Hi Alex, thank you for the positive comments. We are so happy you enjoyed your meal at The Halal Guys and look forward to seeing you again!

We got two combo regular platter for $13 each. Only less than 10 in line and it was served and packed very quickly. My wife and I shared one platter for dinner and they were plenty of food for two. It was tasty and a great value. Highly recommended to any NYC visitors to experience this food adventure.
The food is great and really inexpensive.  We always get at least one meal there when we stay at the Hilton.
Thank you so much for the positive review! We are happy to see you've been pleased with your meal at The Halal Guys!

There is a reason why this place is as popular as it is. This was the first food stop I went to in NYC and I am so glad I did because this was perfect. The experience of waiting in line for a food truck in the middle of a concrete jungle is just so New York. It's a great feeling and vibe to just be part of the city's ecosystem. As for the food itself, I got the chicken gyro with one line of hot sauce and wow. This was amazing. The meat was cooked perfectly with a great seasoning and they just load it in the pita with a whole lot of sauce and toppings. Actually such a good gyro and definitely worth the wait in the line.

Been on my list of places to try and best decision EVER! It was so delicious and tasty! We got the chicken and the gyro, the gyro was a little bit salty but overall really good. It comes with rice (the way they make their rice was really good and a hint of sweet), lettuce, vegetables and the sauces. They pack the food in there and the amount is great to share with 2 or more people. The price is not expensive at all. The service is great. They guys are really nice. They do get busy but the line does go by fast so you are never really waiting long. But it definitely worth the wait. It is a good truck and it's in New York so the ambiance is beautiful since you are eating outside and looking at the beautiful buildings.
Hi Vesta, thank you for sharing your wonderful review about The Halal Guys! We are happy to have served you, please feel free to reach out to our team if you have any additional feedback.

This was our first stop in New York since we got in so late and needed something hot and filling! Make sure you go to the right places there are a lot of carts that'll say "Halal" on it to trip you up. This was a simple, affordable and delicious meal. We got the chicken over rice and it was LOADED. The sauce that comes with it is incredible, be sure to get it. It is cash only so be sure you've got some cash on you before heading over. The line moved quickly and service was super quick as our food was ready within a couple minutes.
This cart in Theater District is the original Halal Guys and a cool visit in NYC if you are a big fan of halal food! While busy, the wait isn't too long. Huge portions and love their combo plate.
Hi Mia, thanks for the 5-star review! We appreciate you taking the time out of your day to rate The Halal Guys.

When in NYC you have the try the original Halal guys. We came here around 9pm and the line wasn't too bad. The total wait time was about 25 minutes, but it didn't feel like it. I forgot how delicious the chicken and rice is here especially with the hot sauce on top. Weather was a bit cold but once you took it bite out of it you instantly felt the warmness. Cool and nice ambiance to eat outside to taste the freshness of it.
Thank you for the 5 star review, John! We're always thrilled to see a satisfied customers share their opinion.

I've passed this cart so many times while wandering Avenue of the Americas. We finally decided to stop here for a mid afternoon savory snack and so happy with the decision. They have a few sizes of bowls and really, I just wanted the meat and sauce and it didn't disappoint. I'm a fan of the spicy red and white sauce and it was the perfect size for $10. Cash and card!

Went late at night (we were actually trying to get Adele's but line was too long lol). I think since they've expanded the quality has been commercialized slightly- it's still very good but I've since seen other halal carts do waaaaay better. I think this is a great baseline comparison halal cart though. I don't know if I'd come back considering all their other better options available
Wanted to see what the hype is. It's a solid choice for a quick lunch. We had a good Gyro mixed chicken ann beef white sauce.
Thank you for being a valued customer! If you have any suggestions on how we can make your experience a 5-star, please reach out and share!

I really wanted my first Halal Guys experience to be from a cart vs a brick and mortar. So I'm glad that I happened to be seeing a show at a theatre just around the corner from this location. As many reviews mentioned, there will always be a line. When we went it was an off time on a weekday so it wasn't too long, but I had still had the foresight to order ahead via their website. Just as I was getting there, I could see one of the employees moving an order to their 2nd cart which is there for mobile pickups. I walked right up, gave them my name, and sure enough, that bag was mine and I was on my way. It couldn't have been easier. The food itself was perfect. Everything tasted fresh. The meat was hot, the veggies were cold and crispy, and the sauces were, well, amazing. The whole meal filled me up without having me feel stuffed. I really appreciated that because I feel like other places will give you the same amount of food but it will be so heavy that you just feel awful after eating it all. So, if you are in the theatre district and want a fresh, flavorful, and filling meal, Halal Guys is a great option.

Wait approx 30 mins on a cold wintery night for Halal guys.. food prices are very reasonable for a quick meal in Manhattan 9-12$. We both ordered 2 combo platters. Hubby had the large $12 combo beef gyro and chicken platter. I had the regular $10 combo chicken falafel platter. Initially looked like it had too much white sauce smothered on top, but tuned out to be the perfect amount. The pita was so nice and soft tender from being steamed in top of the chicken on their grill. Falafel was warm and crispy. Would advise to order ahead on yelp or something if you're in a rush as the line was slow moving. Recommended!
Hi Iris M.! Thank you for taking the time to rate and review us. We are happy to hear of your love for our food and truly appreciate your support. We look forward to your next visit! The Halal Guys
The falafel bowl was overall ok. The red sauce was super spicy and was not a fan of the white sauce. Falafel was crispy but not the best. I prefer moshes falafel.

It's still very tasty after 16 years.  Got the regular but the ratio of meat is too low. Struggling to get a bite of meat with everything else Anyways worth a try if you haven't been.  But it's not the same as before.

Thank you for taking the time to share your thoughts about The Halal Guys! We would love to have the opportunity to connect with you directly about any issues you may have during your experience. If we can connect on areas we've fallen short, we can make changes to better ourselves. Please contact us at your convenience to chat.

I live in CA.  I still think about this cart when I think about food or NY. Wish they would open ones in other states. I had the lamb plate 3 times in my 4 day stay in NYC. The real cart is open during the day on the southeast corner. At night it is on both the southwest and southeast corner. And they have one on 53rd and 7th.  across the street from the sheraton towers. The sauce is way better than any yogurt sauce I've ever had.  And the hot sauce is real tasty too.  Everything is perfect about the lamb plate and if you get the pita.  I think it is more of a flat bread because is real soft and perfect. And it so inexpensive.  And the portions are huge.  My wife and I end up just sharing one plate. The imposters are on the southwest corner during the day.  They have yellow shirts with no logo.  And they don't have the logo on their plastic bags.  They are jerks too.  Someone in their line was leaving their line and I told them the real guys are across the street.  They started going crazy and yelling at me.

THE famous Halal Guys. I've tried it when they franchised to the West Coast. Here was my experience at the actual spot. AMBIANCE: Parking: Not really. Street parking or parking at the Hilton/Sheraton. Seating: Nothing designated but there are benches a few steps away. Vibes: Welcome to Midtown NY! Plenty of iconic spots and places, one being Halal Guys! The spot itself is pretty busy close to Times Square and many Broadway shows. It's nothing too flashy, there are actually a few other Halal Guys carts but you can tell this is the original based on the longer line or being across the Hilton. Great place for a grab and go. FOOD: Combo - Beef/Chicken/Gyro Platter (Recommend) Why not? The best of all worlds! Chicken, beef, and gyro well cooked and flavored, complemented with rice, fresh lettuce, tomatoes, and their signatures sauces. They've grown their flavors but I love the classic cool white sauce, refreshing green sauce, and fiery (really) hot sauce (packaged separately). CUSTOMER SERVICE: Great! Despite the long line they were pretty professional and composed. TL; DR OVERALL: 4.5 Stars. Good price, good selections, and a pleasant experience. This hits! I'm impressed how they still kept it affordable. It's a great bang for your buck too! Glad they franchised but if you happen to find yourself in the area, it's definitely worth a try. #RepresentASIAN TIPS: * You'll actually probably see a few other Halal Guys - the original original one is on 53 & 6 right across from Hilton near a fountain. It actually has a long line but the others are just as great!
Hi Leland, thank you for the positive comments. We are so happy you enjoyed your meal at The Halal Guys and look forward to seeing you again!

Yup, came back almost a year later and I still like this better compared to Adels. Affordable and simple at $12 cash for a Regular. Split it w my SO and it was a perfect amt. SO says meats slightly dry but it didn't bother me. Added a separate white sauce and it was still great. The veggie/rice ratio is perf

Yep, I get the hype. I like the halal guys that I've had in LA but the OG stand just HITS DIFFERENT. Truly legendary. Eaten right away, or heated up  later as a drunk food, all of it is just so so good. Line around 3:40pm was like 10-15 parties deep, but it moves fast. Got our food within 15-20 minutes of waiting in line. A small platter with combo chicken and beef was $10.89. In retrospect I should've gotten a large for an extra dollar to really savor every bite even though I couldn't finish the small in one sitting. I get 3 lines of red sauce, then add another bag. Flavor blast. Burns so good. Meat's not dry. I'm still dreaming about it since ordering it 11/24/24 LOL Service is fast and friendly! The guy took our order quickly, and joked at how I got more lines of red sauce than my dude friend who got one loll

This is the OG and the food is still very good. Got a combo sandwich for $10 cash. Waited in line for about 15-20 minutes. Operations were slow at 5pm. There were only 10-15 ppl in front of me and they took their sweet ass time

Was able to stop by and try The Halal Guys while visiting, my friends and I waited around 5-10 minutes to order and all orders are made to order - staff member was friendly and made the food quickly and added extra white sauce which we enjoyed. Food came out good, delicious - we ordered the beef and complimented with rice, tomatoes, fresh lettuce and sauce.

Ambiance: the food truck is located at the midtown entertainment district, and there's always long waiting line from morning to midnight Service: the line moves slow, as they operate both walk-in and online orders at the same station, expect at least thirty minutes waiting time, once you get to the front line, it's pretty fast to place the order and get your food right away Food: the original and legendary food truck with their simple menu items CHICKEN & BEEF GYRO COMBO - **** the most popular item, lettuce and rice base, topped with chicken and gyro, and pita, sauces are optional, recommend serving with their white creamy sauce and red hot sauce Price: decent potions and cheap prices, less than $15 for a quick bite, it used to be cash only, but they take credit card payment now
I have not tried in a couple of years. The combo is now $12. Portions are smaller, half of it was tomatoes and salad. Still a good deal for $12 but not as much food as before. Lines are also shorter.

Price: $8 as of July 9 at this location. It use to be $7 before this month and $6 in 2013 or 2014. Price as been going up but affordable. It is cheaper than the stores locations where is is $7.99 before taxes for a small and $8.99 for a larger. Wait: There is always a wait no matter if it is lunch time, mid day, dinner time or even midnight. First because of tourists and second because it is cheap filling food after a long night of drinking. Be prepared to wait 5 to 10 minutes. Food: Food is always fresh and hot. If you get a platter, it comes with yellow rice, pita and salad. You can add chicken or gyro or both as meat. I am a frequent visitor when i am by the location. The food i got was really salty. I don't know why. I had trouble finishing it because of that. I will give it another try to see if they have changed their food. Sauce: If you get the platter to go, they are very stingy with the sauce. They charge you more if you want extra. Drinks: They sell drinks. A can of soda is $1. Overall: i would give this a try if you are in the neighborhood, hungry after a night of drinking. It is filling affordable food in NYC.

I first tried the OG Halal Guys cart about 20 years ago, and it was one of those mind-blowing experiences you always remember. Now Halal Guys is franchised, but the franchise locations don't hold a candle to the original experience. So I was hoping to experience that original magic - but sadly the cart was just like the mass produced franchise locations.  The meat was dry, the flavor was lacking, and it was overall a disappointment. I guess it's just one of those things that changes with time!

Hello Nadeem A., We would like to apologize for your recent experience and sorry to hear you were less than satisfied.  We pride ourselves on our service and the high-quality standards we maintain and would like to make things right.  Please reach out to us at rewards@thehalalguys.com to discuss what occurred and how we might make it up to you.

We were introduced to Halal Guys on a previous visit, and now there are a few locations near home in Los Angeles. I tried to find the original cart but couldn't. We made an order, it was only $12 for enough food for both my wife and me! It was very delicious and very filling. The Halal Guys can always be depended on for a good meal!

I stopped by The Halal Guys as I was around the area, since I've heard a lot about them and seen plenty of decent reviews, so I wanted to see what the hype was about. The menu is simple: protein, rice, and salad with three sauces. For protein, they offer chicken, gyro, falafel, or a mix, and you can get it either in a pita wrap or as a platter. Their sauces are white sauce, BBQ, and hot sauce. One thing I like is that they offer two platter sizes -- small for $10 and large for $12. Even though my eyes are big, my stomach is small, so I went with the small platter, and it was the perfect portion. I ordered the combo gyro and chicken and topped it with BBQ and white sauce. It comes with two pieces of pita bread and a little side salad. The meat was decent -- the chicken didn't have much flavor and was pretty bland, but the gyro had a nice texture. The rice was actually pretty good, and the white sauce mixed with the BBQ sauce made the whole dish more flavorful. Overall, I'd rate it a 3.5 out of 5

I was so excited to finally have the Halal Guys tonight after years of MIA. But tonight was definitely a disappointment. I have been eating healthy lately and was extremely excited to finally eat a comfort meal, however the portions were unacceptable. I got the beef platter and it used to come with the perfect amount of salad on the side, but the portion of salad was atrocious. Literally, barely any meat, and the ratio was off. Why am I eating salad AGAIN!!!!???? It wasn't even busy on this rainy day. Who are they saving the meat and rice for? If you're visiting NYC, Halal Guys is definitely not representing us!

Hi Shirley, We're sorry that your experience wasn't what you expected.  At The Halal Guys we strive to provide exemplary customer service to all of our guests.  We would love the opportunity to make it up to you.  Please email rewards@thehalalguysny.com so we can make it right.

Have walked by and saw huge lines here before, so wanted to come back and try. When I did, there was only one couple in front of me. Service was good. Thought the food was good - not great. Would probably stop here again if the line was short.
Customer service was abysmal. No prices listed, food was barely cooked dry and the worst part for 2 chicken over rice and a single kabob we were charged 50+ dollars. this should have been $35

Jason P., We deeply apologize for your experience. It seems like you are disappointed, and we would love to hear more about where we fell short. Please reach out to our customer service team at your earliest convenience. We can be reached at rewards@thehalalguys.com.
One of our favorite spots in NYC. A Must for tourists and locals alike. Food is always delicious and and service is quick. You defenitely get your moneys worth.
Pretty fresh food and delicious it totally fulfilled my expectations in every aspect.
Hi Norman B.! Thank you for taking the time to rate and review us. We are happy to hear of your love for our food and truly appreciate your support. We look forward to your next visit! The Halal Guys
I read this one is the best, so it is where I go when I am in NYC. Once we got this to go, and then went to the Plaza bar for coffee and drinks.
Hi Ceceilia, thank you for the positive comments. We are so happy you enjoyed your meal at The Halal Guys and look forward to seeing you again!

There was a line everyday. I finally stood in it. 10 min, back to front. The front welcomed me with engaging service. $12 FULFILLING and delicious gyro sandwich and alright $6 fries. That sandwich with that sauce...! Yum!

This place is wonderful. I got the falafel platter which was deliciously fresh and tasty. Huge portion sizes. Where else are you going to get a complete dinner in New York City for $11? They worker recommended I try the green sauce which is like the white sauce but a little more herbs. I really liked it. I forgot how good this place was.
Hi Mike, thank you for sharing your wonderful review about The Halal Guys! We are happy to have served you, please feel free to reach out to our team if you have any additional feedback.

You'll try to convince yourself not to do the long line, just like I did, but I caved for my next meal.  Just know that the food is great for the price ($11 for the larger platter they call the "Regular."  Keep in mind that the sandwiches ($9) are also larger that the picture says.  Once you get your food, you can eat it standing up, or try to get lucky and get a spot on the bench outside the building.

It's a rite of passage standing in line at 4am, bleary eyed, maybe a bit drunk, waiting to chow down on some Halal Guys. While I'm waiting and pondering the universe's most mysterious questions, such as how it has taken me over three  decades on Earth to get to this location. All forms of consternation immediately vanished after one bite of my Gyro plate with extra white and red sauces (go easy on the hot sauce...I learned a bit too late that a little goes a long way!).

At some point I think New York was mainly hot dog carts. Now, it's all halal carts. This Yellow shirt classic food stand has been there since 1990. Now this stand typically as a line. They have another stand right across the street. So the concept here is platters. As street food- you have chicken, beef, falafel as options. For my vegetarians, the falafel is made in a separate cart so it can be separated from the chicken and beef. Its made fresh so I had a wait. They came out with 12 piping hot falafels and it was worth it. For the platters you get rice, vegetables and then your protein. In my case, 6 piping hot falafels. On top of it is pita bread and then white and red sauce. The white sauce is a lovely blend of mayonnaise and yogurt. A perfect blending of Mediterranean and American cultures. The red sauce is spicy and should be taken in limited quantities. If you get this to go, they wrap it up for you and put it in a bag. We walked back to the hotel and our food had stayed warm. The rice was flavorful, and the veggies and falafel. Combined with the white and red sauce this was a perfect meal. It cost me $12 + tax. They take cash and card. This line I can be long but what I know is that it's worth it.

Pretty high on the list of NYC legendary carts, and for good reason. I've come to this cart roughly 1-2 times per year since moving to NYC in 2016 and have no plans to stop.  If I lived any closer I'd be here a lot more often. The menu and the process are super simple - get in line no matter who you are (tourist, construction worker, finance bro, marathon runner, other), wait hopefully no more than 5-10 minutes, and then select a platter that comes with rice + meat or falafel. Tell them whether you're OK with the spicy sauce or not; as a guy that genuinely enjoys spicy food, I've screwed around and found out when it comes to their red sauce.  It's delicious but don't overdo it on your first go-round. Pay them $8-$10 for a filling, tasty meal - which in NYC (particularly in Midtown) is an absolute steal. And then enjoy your lunch/dinner/snack on a nearby bench people-watching in the area, or take it to Central Park, or wherever else you want to chow down. I'm not trying to say that this is the best food you'll ever find in New York - but it's so dang reliable in terms of cost and quality, and in one of the most scenic stops in town to boot.  Can't imagine this area without thinking of the Halal Guys cart as well.
Hi Dumond, thanks for the 5-star review! We appreciate you taking the time out of your day to rate The Halal Guys.

The Halal guys have expanded and it's phenomenal to watch. It was a pleasure getting lunch at one of their food carts at the location where it all started. It's a great bang for your buck in the city. 11 or 12 dollars for a plate that is a decent size is a steal in the city. The spicy bbq chicken is indeed spicy so be prepared. The chicken combined with the rice and salad proved to be an satisfying lunch. Halal guys hits the spot in my opinion.

We were so excited to find THE original location of the Halal Guys. We came here on a Sat afternoon around 3pm. Short line but there was always a line! The guys were super nice and didn't rush us to order when we got to the front of the line. They even allowed us to substitute the spicy bbq chicken for the regular chicken in the combo plate. We got two combo plates and a chicken sandwich/gyro. They gave us enough silverware and napkins and extra white sauce and extra hot sauce! Everyone in my group was in agreement that the food and service was 5 stars! We are so happy we stopped by today. The chicken and beef were made to perfection with amazing spices. And the meat combined with the rice and lettuce/tomatoes = amazing! We loved the food and would definitely recommend both the combo dish and the chicken gyro!!!
Hi Miley, thank you for the positive comments. We are so happy you enjoyed your meal at The Halal Guys and look forward to seeing you again!

Still worth the hype! The OG Halal cart, worthy of praise. Not sure why some reviews mention them as having fallen off. Maybe there are better ones, yet the Halal Guys are just as good, generous portions, delicious white and spicy sauce (get both), and enough of a balance between the rice, meat (beef), and vegetables. The falafel was a pleasant surprise, crispy outside and chewy inside. Surprisingly no lamb option. The line can be long.

We waited in line for over 45 minutes in freezing temps and it was worth it! Chicken & rice platter and lamb & rice platters with extra white sauce were ordered and devoured in minutes. What's not to love about consistently delicious food! Tip: Ask for extra white sauce

Visiting First time New York , everyone recommend eating at Halal Guys so we decided check out what all the hype about . Best part getting a wholesome meal at 1 AM at night was really fascinating coming from a town where everything closes at 9 pm. Long Queue at 1 am gave us assurance that food would be delicious. Queue was worth the hype and anyways the queue moved very fast due to the efficiency of the staff. Now the food, We Ordered a few chicken and Falafel Platters which came with rice, lettuce, pita pieces and chicken/Falafel , loaded with the fantastic white sauce. Everything was served super fresh and hot.  Portions were generous. We really enjoyed the food as we were very hungry after a long drive from North Carolina. Slept late with an happy belly ! The Only downside was they only accept Cash  at the food truck . Luckily we had some  it would have been very difficult to  look at cash late night.

Grabbed the combo platter at The Halal Guys 53rd St cart post-theater--juicy chicken/gyro over perfectly seasoned rice with extra white sauce was pure bliss, pita scoopable and filling for $16. Quick despite the line, hot/fresh every time; iconic spot lives up to decades of hype. Must for visitors craving real street eats!
Hi Nicholas, thank you for the positive comments. We are so happy you enjoyed your meal at The Halal Guys and look forward to seeing you again!

Post MOMA yesterday, the quickest dinner to go would be the Halal Guys. Went for a Combo Platter but wanted half of the Chicken to be Spicy Chicken so I can try it. That proved to be a good move as the Spicy Chicken was literally fire, and I have such a high threshold! Combine all the white sauce and hot sauce and it was too hot but soooo good! Glad to see them still holding up. Stay consistent and clean pls! :)
Thank you for taking the time to write a review about The Halal Guys! We are happy to have you as a customer!

Arrived on a Tuesday at 12pm. Wait was about 2-5 minutes and the service was quick. Bring cash as this place, similar to most, takes cash only. The beef gyro is preferred over the chicken and don't forget the red sauce if you're a spicy consumer. I can see the appeal for this spot. If I worked here in nyc, I'd go here often for a cheaper quality meal

Date: Monday, May 6th, 2024 Time: around 9:45pm Party of: 5 What: Dinner or After Drinks Food? Note: Review #10,339 Combo Platter Served with a pairing of (beef gyro, chicken) as well as rice, lettuce, and tomatoes along with your choice of toppings and our famous white and hot sauce. What else can I say about Halal Guys that has not been said?! Deliciously filling cheap eats. The hubby and I shared a platter after a day of drinking and we were good. I can't remember how much it was, but I think it was like $13 or less for a plate of food. And I like how I can add as much white or hot sauce as I want. I do love my food spicy. Combo for me is the way to go since I can have both chicken and beef. I'm not much of a rice person and the hubs is not much of a lettuce person, so it was divide and conquer. We killed that platter. Tasty, affordable, and just yum! REVIEW #3414
Hi Elena, thank you for sharing your wonderful review about The Halal Guys! We are happy to have served you, please feel free to reach out to our team if you have any additional feedback.
Some really good cheap food. A lot of it too. The wait in line was about 45 minutes so don't grab this spot if you're in a hurry. My biggest regret was not getting double white sauce.

When in New York we always grab a bite at the Halal Guys.  Line is always long.  Food  is always consistently delicious.  If it your first time,  you wont regret waiting in that long line because this place always hits!!!! Ask for extra white sauce
Delivery was completed within the estimated time. Food condition was good and nothing was missing. Taste was average and portions were fair. Works well for a quick and simple meal.

Always a line, but always worth it! The guys are always friendly and they pump out the food as quickly as they can. Got 4 chicken platters (for 4 people) with extra white sauce and they were all demolished on the train back north. Always love going to The Halal Guys when I'm in town.
So damn good! we grabbed a couple of bowls here late one night and it was everything you would hope for.

Before this became a chain, the Halal Guys at this location, street side came highly recommended to me by a friend. She was right! There is something really fun and special about dining street side with food purchased from an NYC food cart. Standing there in the cold, I couldn't wait to get food into my belly. Everything was SO good. But, be warned! The hot sauce... it's HOT! Go easy and add slowly to check your spicy temperature limits. I miss NYC! This would be a definite stop if I'm in town. Although, I'm so glad it's become a chain and I'm only 10 minutes away from one of their shops! Not quite the same, charm as being street side.
Hi Juliana, thank you for sharing your wonderful review about The Halal Guys! We are happy to have served you, please feel free to reach out to our team if you have any additional feedback.
For the most part consistent. At least the food is good and the service is polite. The area was quiet.

What can I say about Halal Guys, they are the OG in the chicken and rice game. Pretty much my favorite meal in NY. Nothing better than soaking up the alcohol with delicious seasoned rice and flavorful meats. Just beware of the "hot sauce". Sometimes it's fine sometimes it will leave you crying on 6th street. Always ask for extra white sauce. Getting hungry writing this.
Efficient with lines ( never have to wait more than 20 min for food, unlike adels where they purposely stall the lines) . Food is always amazing and a great options for both kids and adults!
Thank you for the 5 star review, Zukhraf! We're always thrilled to see a satisfied customers share their opinion.

Wait for about 30 minutes on a Wednesday during lunch time (got in line around 12:35 PM and had my food in hand by just after 1:05 PM). While waited in line, seems a lot of food delivery folks from Whizz service came by to pick up delivery orders. The food was good, tasty, reasonable affordable (at least less expensive than in California). However, I'm not sure I'd wait in a line to try this OG cart again. Literally tastes the same as physical store fronts, so the only difference is the experience waiting in line. Very cool first time trying it though!

do not buy their gift cards - a complete and total rip off - i'm out $100 on cards i purchased that never worked and the store on 14th street simply shrugged - bunch of assh###s. i'll never purchase their mediocre crap food again
Hello Theodore L., I’m very sorry we failed to meet your expectations. I would appreciate another chance to earn your business. Please email us at rewards@thehalalguys.com.
Ordered delivery this year. Food was good but loses a touch not eating fresh off the line. Still, feeding 4 adults to fullness for $65 w tip in NYC is a score. Arrived in 1hr via Uber eats.

Line wasn't too bad on a Wednesday afternoon. Wait time was 10 mins. A must stop when in NYC. Unknown Michelin Starred restaurant. $12 for a filling bowl. I only had 9 meals during my time in NYC and this was one of the spots I used it on. Ambiance was great, ate right outside on the benches like a typical New Yorker.
Hi Jeffrey, thanks for the 5-star review! We appreciate you taking the time out of your day to rate The Halal Guys.
Absolutely love this food stand I haven't had it for years but it tasted as yummy as before. The volume and price are unbeatable. Highly recommending it for everyone, especially for tourists.
One of the iconic food trucks in New York City! If you are visiting NYC, don't miss this one! Delicious platters of chicken/gyro/falafel with spiced rice and pita bread.
Thank you for the 5 star review, Shiva! We're always thrilled to see a satisfied customers share their opinion.

WORTH THE WAIT!!! Them guys cooking. The food was lick the fork good. Rice tender. Perfect balance of meat n rice. white sauce good. Hotsauce a bit spicy but good spice notes. I almost wanted to grab a platter to bring home on plane. You gotta give it a try.

The hype is real! Is it worth standing in a long line? YES! We walked to The Halal Guys and approached a long line that we began to stand in, after further investigation we learned we were in the line for Adel's. We kept walking and made it to the right long line, LOL. We probably stood in line for 35-ish minutes. FYI, it was at least 1am in the morning, if not later or earlier, depending on how you look at it. I got the chicken platter, the hubby got the combo platter which comes with chicken and beef. Both dishes were so flavorful, the rice, lettuce, chicken and other accoutrements were a medley of perfection. The pita was warm and fluffy and paired nicely with everything else. The white sauce on top tied everything together. I am SO glad we did not stay in the Adel's line, this was SO much better! Try it! Don't be intimidated by the line. Frankly, New York is a series of lines LOL!
Thank you for the 5 star review, Alison! We're always thrilled to see a satisfied customers share their opinion.

Finally was able to visit and try the original The Halal Guys and it did not disappoint. You won't miss the cart and you will see a long steady line all day but the guys that work here got it down as it moves fairly quickly. Menu is pretty simple. Cash only so be prepared. We ordered chicken platter and get extra white sauce,you'll thank me later. We also got  gyro beef sandwich but I personally like the platter better.If you don't eat spicy the red sauce might be too much for you so try at your own risk. We enjoyed our food somewhere near by the street to make sure we tried it hot and fresh.
Hi Carla, thanks for the 5-star review! We appreciate you taking the time out of your day to rate The Halal Guys.

Some people give Katz a bad rap.  I just finished a half sandwich of Pastrami on rye (seeded) and I'm here to tell ya...."to die for"!  That's coming from a "real" nyker....from the Bronx.  I got the lean and it was n't soggy like some claim.  Let me tell you how I prepared it.  It comes in a sealed plastic bag.  I left it that way as I placed it in a pot of boiling water for 10 minutes.  I toasted the rye bread then smeared both sides with blue cheese salad dressing (brown mustard would be too strong, the meat is flavored enough).  One of the 5 food groups.  The other 4:  Carvel soft serve ice cream, potato knish, and Original famous Ray's Pizza.  All "to die for"!!!!!!

Cash only and prepare for chaos. There will be a line... several.  There 's a line to get in, which is out the door. The doorman hands you a ticket. Keep it. There is a line to order, a line for just drinks, a line for pre-order pick up, and a line to pay. Legit Crazy. Finding a seat to eat is stressful.  I saw a local kick out a non-NYer for saving a table for 6, when all she needed was a table for 2 and she didn't have her food yet. It was crazy. Would I go back... YES!!  There is a line for a reason. That sandwich is amazing!!!!  It was soo huge.  I'm glad the kid and I shared.  The hubs ate the whole thing by himself and had the meat sweats.  Thankfully we walked it off :)

Katz's Delicatessen was my very first stop on my first trip to NYC, and it absolutely lived up to the hype. This iconic spot has been around for generations, serving up legendary pastrami in a classic New York setting. Expect a long line, but it moves quickly. You'll receive a ticket upon entering, have your order marked, and pay on the way out. - Katz's Pastrami Sandwich (on rye) -- incredibly juicy and tender with thick, hand-cut slices piled high; on the pricier side, but worth trying at least once; it's massive and easily shareable, one of the most beautiful pastrami sandwiches I've ever seen The vibe is bustling and full of energy. The walls are lined with old photos that showcase Katz's long history, and the bright fluorescent and neon lights give it that unmistakable deli feel. Beyond pastrami, they also offer classics like corned beef, sauerkraut, and matzo ball soup -- don't forget the pickle to balance everything out. Service is efficient and friendly given the volume. I'm already craving another pastrami sandwich as I write this... Katz's is truly a must-visit NYC staple!

I usually go with the pastrami on rye, sometimes I'll throw Swiss on it. It's stacked, juicy, and exactly what you want from a classic deli sandwich. What makes it even better is the history. Katz's has been around since 1888, and it's one of the last old-school Jewish delis still doing it at that scale in NYC. It's been in the same Lower East Side spot for well over a century, serving generations of New Yorkers, immigrants, and everyone in between. Even the interior still has that worn-in counter-service vibe that feels unchanged on purpose. Pastrami here is consistently amazing. I end up going at least once a month because nothing else really hits the same.

Try: Corned Beef Reuben! Why: Pastrami is obviously delish here and I've had it various times but finally tried their Corned Beef Reuben and it was melt in your mouth goodness! Notes: Came with my parents for late breakfast and it was already busy. Got our tickets at entrance and I went to sandwich line immediately while my parents grabbed a table. Don't forget to tip your butcher esp if they give you a sample. If you're sharing family style, keep all your tickets even unused ones so you can give them back the tickets at exit after paying. Credit card accepted in back counter. Front counter is cash. Ordered too much food? Get it wrapped and bagged in back counter too. Def a staple NYC establishment and dining experience.

In a word, disappointed. I've been wanting for years to go to the famous Katz Deli. Maybe I hyped it up too much. I don't know. We arrived promptly at 11 o'clock on a Saturday morning and there was almost no line. You go in the door, you get one ticket for every person and it's extremely important that you keep that ticket even if there is nothing written on it. Then you hop in the line for whatever it is that you're needing whether it would be a sandwich or hotdog a soda, etc. Then you get in that corresponding line. After you get your food you do not pay at that time. We were lucky enough to find a table right away. Now for the food. We both got corned beef with spicy mustard. The sandwiches look amazing! The meat was hot and it was thick and they had trimmed most of the fat away which I love. The problem is there's almost no taste. It's like steamed meat and the spice is a wish and a dream. A whisper of spice if you will. The pickles were terrible! If you can see my pictures, you can see that one is a dark green and one is a bright green. The dark green ones could be something that you pick off of a grocery store shelf and the bright green one tasted like you just cut up a cucumber and put it in vinegar with maybe a little salt For two sandwich sandwiches, extra pickles and two diet Pepsi's the bill came up to $63 and some change. To be honest, we have a great sandwich place back in Indianapolis, Indiana called Shapiro's and Shapiro's is by far better and at least five times better than Katz. If you don't have a deli by where you live, maybe this will be amazing because you have nothing to compare it to. I do and this was not worth it. I'm glad that I tried it though because if I didn't, I would've always wondered. You should definitely try Katz's at least once, but don't get your hopes too high. Seems more like a tourist trap.

I got lucky and there was no line when I went. While waiting, they even gave out samples of pastrami to try--omg, it was so tender, juicy, and good. I just ordered the classic pastrami sandwich with mustard, and got their spicy sauce on the side. The sandwich was huge and packed with meat. Honestly, it was the best food I had in NYC while I was there.

I was so excited to try THE SPOT when in NYC and was completely disappointed. The line outside moved pretty fast but it's the line inside that was so so slow. I ordered what people recommended which was the pastrami on rye with mustard and Russian dressing on the side, juicy. The meat was DRY, no fat at all. I see online afterwards that you have to tip $20 to get more and better cuts of meat. The sandwich is already $30, tipping another $20 on top of that is utterly ridiculous. I really don't get why they're so famous because the food is just blah. The Hat on the west coast is much better and the meat much juicier and they don't require a big tip to serve you good food. Hopefully this is the only tourist trap we fall for this trip.

Was this a delicious sandwich? YES Did it satisfy my 2:30 AM hunger after drinking? YES Was it amazing and did it change my life? Absolutely not. I finally tried Katz's after seeing the ridiculous amount of online hype over the years of everybody raving about this place. I think this is one of those places where I had too high of expectations going into it and I was let down. This was a great sandwich, although very expensive. They definitely need to fix the bread situation. They need to get thicker or sturdier bread for the sandwiches because it falls apart completely after the first bite. Pickles were good. I honestly don't see myself ever going out of my way to come here again, but wouldn't be mad if I stopped by while in the area next time.

Disclaimer, I am normally not a pastrami fan but I wanted to see if anything has changed. Knowing that Katz is known for their pastrami,  I hoped it would change my perception of what it could taste like or be. We ordered the pastrami sandwich and the matzo ball soup. I have mixed thoughts on the sandwich, some of it had juicy, tender bites but other bites were salty and dry. The matzo ball soup was unique and I liked it, but it was too salty for me. I was in desperate need of water after having both together. The line is long but it moves relatively quick, make sure you go in the lines that have a large tip jar. It means they are likely to move quick and get the food out faster. It was my first time and I learned that you take a ticket, order, eat, then pay. You also have to take a ticket even if you're not ordering, or else pay a lost ticket fine Overall, it was decent. I would try it because it's iconic to NY but I wouldn't go out of my way for it.

Tried Katz' Deli during our trip to NYC! Lots of other tourists were there taking photos. You go in and order at one of the counter lines. Everyone who enters gets a ticket (when you place your order they write it down on the ticket). You bring your ticket to the exit counter and pay there. My husband and I got a full pastrami sandwich and it was way too much for two people! Gigantic mega portions of pastrami meat. The pastrami meat was deliciously fatty and well seasoned but way way more ratio of meat to bread than necessary (which is probably why they are so famous). You could probably feed two people with just a half sandwich. If we had a fridge in our hotel we would've brought more of the meat home and just buy extra bread to eat it with! Tasty but also probably ridiculously fatty

Confusing to figure out what to do. We stood outside in the long line at 3pm on a Friday. Once we got to the door we were given the choice of counter ordering or waiter service. Counter looked confusing and crowded and I was unsure of the process so we were then directed to a new line to wait for waiter service. I thought we came at the "right" time but when we left at about 4:30 or 5:00 the waiter service line was non existent. Overall I think we waited an hour. Food was great. All of it. Bought some merch as we left. Legendary dinner.

We're glad you enjoyed your first visit! And though it can be challenging to predict the line, the best times to try dodging the crowds are generally during off-peak hours: breakfast, between lunch and dinner, or late nights on the weekend. We hope to get another chance to serve you up the perfect sandwich - maybe in a slower setting!

The wait time here can be very long with wait times being more than a hour. It definitely gives the classic NY vibe with the lively and straight up atmosphere. You can even try out the meats before you decide what you want, but you should tip the worker. I got the pastrami sandwich which is definitely a must try and was worth the wait. It's definitely big enough to share between two people. The pickles went well with the meatiness of the sandwich. The meat was tender and savory. The Dr. Brown sodas were refreshing and went well with the meal. Definitely would come back again. It is definitely worth the hype.

Food was great. Ordering process was obnoxious. When you walk in they hand each person a ticket (even if you are ordering together). In order to exit, each person must present your ticket that is marked with prices from each station you order at. Even if you don't order, you must present your blank ticket or you have to pay $50 to exit. We had to order fries at one station, drinks at another and then the soup and sandwich at a third. Once you get your trays of food you have to stalk the tables until you find people getting up. The bussers are on the ball and clear and clean tables quickly. I wish I knew before I had already ordered, but there was a section in the back for table service which I would have opted for had I known. After waiting in line to pay, the person at the register by the door was cash only. I had to return to the back of the store and push through people again to pay. It was chaos. I'm sure it works for them and they make endless money. But from the customer aspect it was not great. The pastrami reuben and motzah ball soup was yummy. The fries were good and the pickles of course were my favorite.

I had went to Katz Deli all the time way before my yelp years and it was always a vibe stroking into a Time Machine with all the old time decor and styles of the deli. I happened to be in the area and couldn't fight the craving for a nice pastrami on rye with a nice bit of mustard and those amazing pickles. It's always a vibe and the great cutters providing a great service cutting that amazing pastrami right in front of you. I could've left with the sample and called it a day. But I took my order to go and had a feast when I got home.

There's usually a huge line but luckily around 9:30pm on a Friday the line was not out the door! Large with many cutters ready and even though the line wasn't out the door it was still incredibly busy inside and took maybe 30 minutes to get our food still Pastrami on rye with cheese and Russian - actually very good! Meat was hit and juicy and tender, cheese was pully too! Sauce was good and matched well but it was very very heavy. I think it's hard to even finish half but definitely yummy 3.5/5 Dr brown black cherry soda - basically a little bit sweeter strong cherry coke maybe mixed with Dr Pepper flavor! Was good but not too unique 3.25/5 Not a fan of the corned beef. Too dry

While on a business trip in NY, everyone has been telling me that Katz is a MUST! There is only one location and I was shocked to see how full this restaurant is! The place was busy, but very organized. It can get noisy due to the number of people dining in at the same time. Upon entering you'll be given a ticket which will be your tab. There are several ordering lines and all turn it around very quickly. The servers give you a generous sample of Pastrami of which Katz is known for. Ordered the Pastrami Sandwiches and Matzo Ball soup. Sandwich was huge, good for 2 servings! Pickles are a must! Hands down the BEST Pastrami I have ever had! As the people next to me would say that Katz is the Church of Pastrami! Definitely will come back again. Highly recommend if ever in NY! You can't find anything close to it!

"Ask, and ye shall receive!" We've all known that Katz's is one of those New York City landmark that is world famous. Especially that scene in 'When Harry Met Sally' with Meg Ryan and Billy Crystal. I'll have what she's having. My best friend was in New York recently and he was texting us photos. Subsequently, he sent us photos of the sandwiches from Katz's. I jokingly replied, "Where's mine?" He texted back,"Brisket or Pastrami?" And further asked what kind of cheese I wanted. I replied  that I was joking and if he was serious. To my surprise (not really), he said that he was going to get one for me prior to returning home the following day. Sheeesh. Now, I haven't been to New York and this has definitely been on my bucket list for the longest since the 80's. The anticipation of finally getting my hands on their famous Pastrami Sammich was palpable. When he finally arrived and handed me the bag, I had plenty of emotions that I couldn't describe. As I gently unwrapped the wax paper, this thing was definitely hefty. Now, it may not have been in the best shape as it just traveled 5 hours across the country, but it still looked pretty decent. I had to give it a few minutes in the air fryer before finally tasting it and it was satisfying. No, I didn't get the same reaction as Meg Ryan did, but overall, it was a solid Pastrami Sammich. Now, I'm fully aware that it would be best to consume it freshly-made, but the sandwich held up. The meat was fatty, juicy and flavorful. But what surprised me the most were the sides of pickles that came along with it. I'm not a fan of pickles, mind you. But these pickles had a nice, crisp, sharp tang to it that complimented the sandwich splendidly. I can't fully say I can cross this off my bucket list now since I know I'll have a different experience eating it there. But I was appreciative of my friend by providing me with that experience of finally having the privilege of gettin' this in mah belly. On a side note: Langer's in LA is still my best rated Pastrami Sammich to date.

Pastrami here is a must- off the bone meat so soft and tender. Tends to be long but if you go off hours (ex. later in the night) no real line but line does move during the day. Little scattered ordering process but so so good and worth- defs a must try
This place is such a classic- good quality meat and lots of food. Can be a long wait but just have to time it right. Really good sandwiches. Definitely recommend. Nice homey vibes

I knew enough about Katz's Delicatessen to know that their sandwiches are big and it would be a good idea to head out here with a dining companion. I was right. What I didn't know was that unless you wanted to head deep in and to the right for a seat in their table service area, that it was the hunger games in here. But first, we had to wait to get in.  This was the easy part.  At 2:12pm on a weekday, we waited in a line just over 10 minutes to enter their doors. Each person received a pink ticket.  Don't lose it.  They charge a minimum if you lose one, even if it was blank.  And they count your tickets as you leave, should you have paid in the back already. With ticket in hand, this is what you should do - each person in your party should tackle one of the following, by proximity order: soup head over to the first line which is right most; sandwich with pickles, head to a cutter line, drinks and sides, that's the line left of the numerous cutter stations, for dessert, ask one of the folks on either side of the cheesecake case, who will also take your money when you are done, and if you have a spare person, they can go table hunting. My cutter line was a little slow as he got tasked with take out order prep, but he was really nice! Note: cutters have tip jars. This was my first pastrami sandwich.  The meat was hot and tender!  I let them add microwaved melted cheese (for a charge) to it along with the mustard.  There's more mustard on the table!  As well as ketchup and napkins.  The pickles were two sort, and included in the price.  Dull green were true pickles.  The ones that looked more fresh tasted like they were just soaked in water, but I ate it in conjunction with the pickled pickle to lighten things up.  My DC wanted the matzo ball soup.  It ended up hitting the spot to bring comfort to the tummy in company to the sandwich. To finish, I grabbed a slice of cheesecake when the line had died down.  No graham cracker crust here!  Just your average tasty creamy cheesecake. After tax, we two got out the door for $53.19 and our two pink tickets stapled on. (And ripped off at the door.)

Wow. I- I didnt know pastrami could be like this. Like the dude was cutting it and I was like do they have a really good knife or am I seeing pastrami sashimi'in right in front of my eyes?? TOURIST LUCK in coming here and there was no line!! No crowd!! Yipee! First off, amazing system. I wish we had it for tacos here. Its a bit confusing if you've never been but u go in and get a ticket, line up anywhere to get your deli sandwich, they write on it what you get, and then you eat and enjoy it and pay the ticket out the door. So efficient. Inside is spacious, full of history/culture, and lots of seating. Kind of like a school lunch room and a grandpa's living room had a baby. The pastrami I was in shock when the man started cutting it, literally sliced down like butter. They give a piece to sample and are very efficient with the sandwich. I ate it and instant mind blown. Like I couldn't believe how tender it was, that pastrami could be so thick yet melt so easily. It wasnt too salty and full of flavor. But best of all, omg the pickles and cucumbers was just that craving that I can never hit in California. Not sweet, soo crunchy, perfectly sour. Taking the pieces of meat that fell out of the pile of the sandwich and wrapping it around the cucumber- absolute perfection. The sandwiches are pricy but we shared it nicely amongst 3 people and it could be stuffed amongst 2. If I were to go again, I'd ask for extra pickles.
A trip to the city is never complete without Katz's.. It'll give you the meat sweats but it's worth it! Be patient, tip your cutter, and enjoy!

What a line to get in! We opted for table service over self service. It's bustling in there for sure. I had a half Ruben and a half side salad. I removed the bread and opted to eat it with a knife and fork because it's so large. I needed a steak knife to cut the meat but only had a butter knife. Wouldn't go again.

What an amazing experience. The sandwiches are expensive - but are enough to feed two people. My daughter and I got a pastrami with sauerkraut and cheese, and a side of macaroni salad, with a water and a black cherry soda.  Our total was $48 before tax, and we were very full. This was our first time and ordering is a little confusing, but there direct you to one of the cutters to get started.  I was asking questions and my cutter may have been trying to be funny and witty, but since it was my first time I genuinely did not know if he was joking or not. I would have preferred a non sarcastic answer as I was new. The food was nothing short of AMAZING. The best, most creamy Mac salad I've ever had, and this was also my very first pastrami sandwich of my life.  I recommend getting the Russian sauce on the side and then you can mix between the Russian and the mustard that is sitting on the table. I equally liked them both .  I don't think I got the full experience of trying different meats because the cutter was not helping me. Don't skip this - worth the time and money, but I hope you get a more helpful cutter. (And yes, I tipped him s as suggested).

We're so glad that you and your daughter enjoyed your first visit! And though part of our charm for many of our customers is our "old-school New York" attitude, it's never meant to be rude - just schtick. We’d love to have you come in and experience the food without the attitude, and hope you’ll be back for another pastrami and macaroni salad fix!

Wow. Amazing, was so excited to try and it did not disappoint! The pastrami is the best I have ever had. Super efficient counter service with many lanes to get food made in front of you, and a very awesome vintage vibe. Only knock was they only had Pepsi products

Very tourist spot but definitely worth trying in my opinion. Super busting they give you a ticket upon entry and you checkout using the ticket as you leave. Losing the ticket is a $50 fee lol. Pastrami is cooked incredibly well, falls apart as you bite it. Definitely an expensive sandwich but big enough to share among a couple people. Plenty of seating even though it's so crowded. I think I will be back in the future!

We're so glad you enjoyed your first visit - we love making new fans! And though we often serve a packed house, if you ever want to try dodging the crowd, drop by at an off-peak hour: breakfast, between lunch and dinner, or late nights on the weekend. Hope to see you back again soon for round two!

Had the pleasure of having dinner at Katz with a Katz family member. Had the standard pastrami on rye. It was not overloaded because I forgot to bring cash to tip the meat cutter. The pastrami was delish with the signature Katz flavor and hand cut. My friend ordered two hot dogs and a knish. All were great including the house pickles. Is Katz that much better than all the other delis in NYC probably not but its something you must do atleast once when visiting. Its a right of passage. PS. Its always better to bring cash.

100% best pastrami sandwich. Our 1st time in NY & we researched the best spot to try one of these sandwiches & this place was mentioned the most. TIP: the line literally wrapped around the building so we saw somebody suggest to go on Uber Eats and order through there for a pick up, which is what we did so we did not have to wait in line for half an hour or longer. There was a park nearby that we sat down at to eat it.

So very disappointed!  The great days of Katz's Deli is definitely behind us.  The food has NO flavor and I didn't enjoy paying $30 for a corned beef sandwich that was fatty and tasteless.  The pictures speak volumes - stale french fries, limp pickles and baked beans that were inedible.  It just feels like they're resting on their history which is So sad!  My honest advice, skip the long lines and avoid this place.

Lunch time, Yes, Yes, Yes! IYKYK. One of our friends was dying to go here as a first timer; never disappoints, it's busy as usual; I went with a half pastrami sandwich and chicken soup. Agree it was tasty, one of the the deli guys gives you a sample cut of the pastrami to enjoy while you wait for your order. Good experience. Pricey, touristy vibe, fabled setting - walls are covered with celebrities photos taken with owner and workers. Keep in mind, cash only, there is an ATM machine in the back. I would be a repeat customer. Stick with Pastrami order,  food moves, not sits.

We're so glad to hear your friend enjoyed their first visit - there’s nothing we love more than making new fans! And though cash is the easiest way to check out, we do also accept credit cards at the back of the store near the water station. Hope to see you all back again soon for another soup and sandwich fix!

Waited around 30 minutes on Thursday evening. Pastrami sandwich was very yummy. Meat was tender and flavorful and went well with the Swiss cheese and onions. Unfortunately the bread completely fell apart so I needed to eat it with a fork. The half pickled light green pickle was absolutely disgusting I couldn't even eat it. The other pickle was good. Great old school atmosphere.

We’re glad to hear you enjoyed your pastrami, but are sorry you were disappointed by part of your visit! Those pickles were most likely half-sours - also known as “new pickles” - which are brined for less time and therefore taste more like snappy, fresh cucumbers. That being said, we never want any customer to feel dismissed or less than thrilled by the quality of their meal - we thank you for your honest feedback and hope you’ll drop by again sometime!

A New York classic and must stop dining option when in NYC! While the line may be long, don't let it deter you from going. The line is pretty quick and we were inside in about 30ish minutes we do opt to wait a little longer and went to the back for table service, but I was told the way to do it is order from the deli counter. Katz was able to accommodate a large party of 7 for all of us to dine together. While the table seating area is significantly smaller than the deli area, still a great option to sit, relax and grab a bite. I ordered the half pastrami sandwich and matzo ball soup. This was WAY more than I anticipated ordering for food. The half sandwich was stacked high with pastrami, and it was the best pastrami I've ever had. The matzo ball soup was piping hot and everything I needed for the cold winter day of touring. We also had a couple plates of the half and full soup pickles. Totally worth trying both. I liked the crispness of a half sour pickle but the full sour had its own kick to itself. Katz's website does have a shipping option so I might have to figure out how long shipping is to have some pastrami sent here to the west coast. I cannot wait to come back for more in the future!

We're so glad you enjoyed your first visit! Though we do often serve a full house, if you ever want to try dodging the wait, drop by at an off-peak hour: breakfast, between lunch and dinner, or late nights on the weekend. And if you're ever craving a West Coast pastrami fix, we offer free two day shipping nationwide on all orders over $100! Hope to see you back again next time you're in town.

Ok, I didn't have high expectations for this place because of how popular and touristy it is but damn their pastrami was good. Definitely the best pastrami I have ever had, and I love pastrami and get it often whenever I see it on the menu. Also tried the  potato knish, which was not bad either. The pickles were great too. The chocolate egg cream was alright, I enjoyed jt, just nothing too special I guess, tasted kind of like a little fuzzy cold cocoa drink. The pastrami sandwich was pretty big so I'd suggest splitting if you are not too hungry, the two of us only got one sandwich and one knish to share and it was enough food. Needless to say, definitely recommend. And get the pastrami on rye.

Got the half sandwich with soup!! Split pea soup was nice, chicken noodle soup was typical. Wish both were hotter in temperature though. Pastrami sandwich was so delicious!! Tender, flavorful and fatty! Fries are huge and filling. Gets super packed all the time. Plenty of seats but may be hard to find. Table service is offered! Service is kind and quick.

We're so glad you enjoyed your first visit! And though we do often serve a full house, if you ever want to try dodging the crowd, drop by at an off-peak hour: breakfast, between lunch and dinner, or late nights on the weekend tend to be less crowded. Hope to see you back again soon for another soup and sandwich fix!

A classic and chaotic NYC establishment! Perhaps not the best pastrami I've had in my life, but a darned good one piled high and served with mustard on soft bread! The fries came recommended by the butcher but I would skip in favor of a different side! Despite a busy evening, the staff was friendly and helpful, but finding seating may be difficult! There are several lines so be sure to move in in order to keep things efficient.

I love beef tongue but it is very hard to find sliced beef tongue in a deli. After discovering that Katz makes beef tongue sandwich, I went back. I arrived around 8 AM and it was still empty. I went to the cutter without waiting in line. It took a very delicious. It tasted s tender and not too salty. I really savor it. It's a huge sandwich for one sitting.

We're so glad to hear you enjoyed your visit! And yes - though we often serve a full house, the best times to try dodging the crowds are definitely during off-peak hours: breakfast, between lunch and dinner, or late nights on the weekends. Hope to see you back again soon!

I highly recommend coming here early to avoid the crowds. I got here around 7:30 AM and there were short lines at three cutter lines. Upon arriving, the guard gives you a ticket that you need to give to the cutter for your order. Do not loose it because you need it to pay and to go out. You need to give the ticket back to the guard. Prepare some cash for tipping the cutter. He will give you several pieces of the meat to taste. . You can leave the tips by Venmo by scanning the code on the tipping cup. I had the pastrami sandwich. The cutter gladly packed half of the sandwich to go because I asked for a bag . He put some pickles, mustard, wood spoon for spreading, and some napkins. The meat is soo juicy and tender. Amazing. It's expensive but you can make two sandwiches with the meat that they put. Plenty of seatings including the seats from Harry Met Sally. All around the walls you can see pictures of celebrities. Definitely an iconic establishment to visit in NYC

It's delicious but overpriced! Enjoyed everything though - pastrami, fries, pickles -- only thing that wasn't good was hot dog. Very historic spot and ok staff - some were amazing others are very old school utilitarian.  Would recommend Langers in LA for similar price and much better!

This was definitely an experience, and now that I've checked it off I'm not sure I need to again. Loved the deli experience and although always busy they are a well oiled ship! We shared a pastrami sandwich and it was definitely the best move due to price and size of the sandwich. Their rye bread was soft and complemented the meat well. The meat was tender and we enjoyed the mustard. If you love huge meat heavy sandwiches you'll love this spot, it just wasn't my cup of tea. I enjoyed the experience much more than the food, but the food was solid just nothing I'd go out of my way for again.

This place is an iconic deli that can clearly get busy. I arrived on a Saturday morning, right when they opened. There was no line, but I got a sense this place is made for lines. I ordered a pastrami sandwich, extra pickles, matzo ball soup, and a root beer. The system with ordering/tickets/where to get certain items is somewhat confusing. Keep your ticket! The sandwich was good, but I wish it had more mustard. The matzo ball soup was delicious. and the pickles were fresh. Everyone had the super charming New York service (just kidding). I just wish the purchase system wasn't super confusing.

We're so glad you enjoyed your visit! And yes, though we often serve a full house, the best times to try dodging the crowds are during off-peak hours: breakfast, between lunch and dinner, or late nights on the weekends. Now that you know the ropes, hope to see you back again for round two!

The Pastrami on Rye lived up to every bit of the hype. It was easily one of the best sandwiches I've ever had--perfectly seasoned and packed with flavor. A few tips for your visit: - The Wait: The line is long around lunch! Bring a podcast or a friend to keep you company. - The Stations: When you get your ticket, head toward the cutting stations in the back. Most people crowd the ones near the front door, so you'll usually find a shorter line further in. - The Tip: Definitely tip your cutter! They'll often give you a slice or two to taste while they prep your sandwich. - The Seating: It's a bit hectic and first-come, first-serve 'family style.' Just grab a spot where you can find one. Overall, the atmosphere is busy and chaotic in the best way possible. Grab a pastrami on rye with mustard, some pickles, and enjoy!

Visited New York this past weekend, and it was everything I imagined! Katz's Delicatessen was high on my list of places to try, and it did not disappoint. We took the subway there, which was an adventure in itself. When we arrived, there was a short line, but it moved quickly. While waiting, you can watch through the windows as sandwiches are made and the meats are cooked and sliced--it's truly a sight to see. Once inside, you're given a ticket and told not to lose it (seriously--don't lose it!). There are multiple lines for sandwiches, and it took us about 20 minutes to reach the front. At the counter, they give you samples of corned beef and pastrami. The pastrami completely sold me, so I ordered the Reuben--and it was incredible. Hot, flavorful, and perfectly balanced with that crunchy sauerkraut. There's a separate counter for fries and drinks, and seating is cafeteria-style. We ended up sharing a table with strangers, which felt totally normal in that environment. When you're done eating, you pay at another counter--and you must have your ticket. I saw someone lose theirs, and they were told they'd have to pay $50 to replace it. They wouldn't even give him his sandwich--definitely a tough lesson learned! The food was so good that on my way home, I ordered pastrami from their website. It arrived in three days and tasted just as amazing. Katz's is absolutely worth the hype (and the price). If you're in NYC, it's a must-visit!

I like this place. Everything about it feels very "New York"...from standing in line outside in the freezing cold on a January afternoon, to the employees helping you/yelling at you at the same time; what a quintessential & iconic NY experience! Obviously I came for the famous pastrami sandwich. For $29, it comes with nothing but the meat + bread ($28.95 to be exact) but you can add to it (for extra $) if you want (I added cheese). If you eat inside, a plate of sour & half sour Katz homemade pickles is served as a "mini-appetizer" and a bottle of Katz mustard is on every table. The pile of pastrami on this sandwich is not only HUGE, but it *IS* as delicious as the hype claims it to be! Putting the Katz mustard on it only made it better!! I think it's worth waiting in line for (it moves quicker than expected) if you're looking for a very authentic NY-style Jewish deli experience :)

Lineup and get a ticket.  The place is packed, huge, and happy people eating pastrami sandwiches throughout the building.  We got the cheesecake and sandwich and grabbed a seat.  Checked my Harry Met Sally orgasm scene photo and even bought an apron.  Happy Yelping!

Long line, don't worry! It's so fast! Welcome to the entry door. Where a nice 6'5 man will hand you a ticket that he urges you not to lose, or drop, to hold while in line and then use to pay. We did just that! Held on for dear life and got assigned to a line (move over and move forward). After that start enjoying just look around, take it in. Stand quietly and just watch the room move around you from the hustle and bustle of the meat guys waking back and forth, cutting pastrami, laughing with the customer in front of them and eachother. You'll catch yourself smiling among the 100 people standing inches from you! Get to the front counter and those meat men (butchers), not sure what to call them but, they are the kindest silliest people! Walk up with a smile, feed that tip jar and they will give you a nice piece of pastrami to try in line as you wait for your food! They prep everything right in front of you. Once presented with your food walk over and find a seat, DO NOT SEPARATE FROM YOUR FRIEND AND GO FIND A SEAT. Just grab your food, grab your side, grab your drink and then, go find a seat. There will be a space, just breathe. Tables are wiped down and reset seconds after someone stands up. If you don't like people bumping you, don't go here. If you love NYC , pastrami, pickles, and nostalgia, GO HERE . Pickles 1000/10 Pastrami 10/10 French fries 10/10

My family was in town and consequently I had been wanting to go back to Katz's for awhile... perfect timing! I strolled over around 11:15am, Thursday in January and almost walked right by it because there was nobody on line, which is what I was expecting to see to mark my arrival. We decided on table service (order by waiter instead of counter. You still get a ticket, don't lose it!). Within about 30 minutes the restaurant was  full. There is something so special about the thick carved juicy pastrami, with just the best amount of fatty bits of meat, on rye bread with mustard... enjoying the buzz of the restaurant and examining the fabulous photos of celebrities on the wall. I couldn't believe that we were sitting next to a photo with Rob Reiner! $28.95 plus tax for pastrami sandwich. Fries or knishes or any other sides extra, go for it!

Hard to believe that I've lived in NYC for over 20 years and I finally ate my first pastrami sandwich from Katz!  No real excuse for this late experience, especially since I head down to the Lower East Side/ East Village frequently... maybe it's the long lines or the other amazing food options available downtown that delayed my purchase? While I don't eat pastrami or corned beef often, I have Second Avenue Deli and Sarge's as closer options to me when I have a craving. With a little extra pandemic time on my hands, I strolled down to East Houston with Katz's being my planned destination... midweek, around 3:45pm, of course there was still a line, but not that bad. I had the nicest guy carve my sandwich... he had just started his shift about an hour earlier so his carving arm was fresh and not over worked yet... we joked about the first timers who wait on line for a hamburger or cheese sandwich... or ask for ketchup on their corned beef.  But I guess that's not completely fair, because you also go to Katz's for the tradition and old world charm. Lean pastrami on rye, mustard on the side and sour pickles. I had each half wrapped separately and grabbed a table to eat half there. $27.16 including tax. Juicy aka standard pastrami which has more fat is $2 less.

WHEN HARRY MET SALLY - Katz's took off!  Although it's been around since 1888. Over many years going back to childhood I can remember my dad bringing us here.  We would always order the iconic Pastrami on Rye with mustard. Nothing else for me. The sandwich has enough meat packed into it, that it can last me 3-4 meals. Maybe two meals for you guys. My dad liked their Matzo Ball soup and hot dogs too. Lately there are lines going outside the block, so be patient. The pastrami sammie now costs $31.00. Yes, it is pricey. I remember when it was an even $20.  No worries, we only visit once in a blue moon.  Tourist attraction as we New Yorkers know, Katz's is Iconic. Wishing you all a Healthy Happy Peaceful New Year 2026! Thank you Rob Reiner - Rest in Heavenly Peace

Lunch with the team at the legendary Katz's Delicatessen... and suddenly we weren't coworkers anymore -- we were gladiators fighting for pastrami. Since 1888, this place has been slicing meat by hand, and you can hear it the second you walk in -- knives thwacking, neon glowing, people yelling orders like it's Wall Street but with mustard. Chaos? Yes. Beautiful? Also yes. Pro move: tip the cutter a couple bucks... and suddenly you're getting bonus pastrami like you just unlocked a secret level.
