The team went all in: * Hand-carved Pastrami on Rye (mandatory NYC citizenship test) * Brisket + American Cheese on Italian bread (built like a linebacker) * Turkey Lettuce Tomato w/ mayo (for the guy pretending to be healthy) * Half-sour & Full-sour pickles (garlic bombs of happiness ) And yes... we found the famous table from When Harry Met Sally -- but nobody recreated the scene... because our mouths were too full. Also survived the legendary ticket system. Didn't lose it. Felt like I completed a New York survival course. Katz's isn't just lunch... It's a rite of passage. It's history. It's meat stacked higher than your Monday stress. Real New Yorkers don't count calories... We count layers of pastrami.
We're so glad that you and your coworkers enjoyed your visit - sounds like you held your own in the pastrami arena! Hope to see you back again soon for round two.

C'mon it's Katz! Worth the hype, worth the wait! I get pastrami on rye with Swiss cheese and dressing on the side. Also the fries and potato knishes are Service is excellent and organized. Plan for the experience to be a bit chaotic, but that's what makes it fun!

Katz's is the famous "Harry Met Sally" place but it is even more justifiably famous for its awesome sandwiches. We came here for the classic Pastrami on rye. It is awesome and big and easily enough for two normal eaters. Of course, if you're a football player or teenage boy you may want a whole one to yourself. We got two of these bad boys for the four of us as well as some Cole slaw and a bunch of pickles. Set us back over $70, including tax, etc. Cash preferred (they can do CC but it's more of a PIA and I think it costs more). All said, great food - I like it better than my former fave (Schwartz's) - pics say it all.

"I came here wanting to see if the hype was real, and honestly? Believe the hype. I'm probably biased because When Harry Met Sally... is my favorite movie, but even setting the movie magic aside, this place is legendary for a reason. The sandwiches are truly to die for. The pastrami is tender, piled mile-high, and absolutely worth every penny. It's everything you want in a classic New York deli experience. Go for the food, stay for the history and the atmosphere, you won't be disappointed!
We're so glad to hear you enjoyed your first visit - hope to see you back again soon for round two!

So good! Upon entering, it can be a bit disorienting where to go. The deli place reminds me of that scene in New Girl where the MC is trying to order a sandwich and its all chaos. There are two lines: one for sandwiches and one for sides and drinks. My partner and I decided to divide and conquer. We got their popular pastrami sandwich, and it was melt-in-your-mouth delicious! The sandwiches are huge, so do share. Was so crestfallen to see the two persons sitting near us leave their unfinished sandwiches behind. What a waste! The sandwiches come with some cucumbers/pickles, which was the perfect palate refresher after all that fatty goodness. In addition to the sandwiches, we also ordered some potato latkes and the matzo ball soup. Complete satisfaction. Definitely a taste of local flavor and a must stop if you're in New York.

Glad to hear you had a great visit! And though we definitely enjoy a little chaos, if you want to try dodging the crowds for your next pastrami fix, drop by at an off-peak hour: breakfast, between lunch and dinner, or late nights on the weekend. Hope to see you back again soon!

A tourist destination that lives up to the hype! Yes it is expensive but you pay for the experience and history. Plus the pastrami sandwich is actually really really good! Actually avoided the line by going in right when they opened. Nothing wrong with pastrami for breakfast! The meat was so tender and not overly salty. Definitely worth it for a one and done experience.

We're so glad you enjoyed your visit - we love making new fans! And yes, though we often serve a full house, the best times to drop by are definitely during off-peak hours: breakfast, between lunch and dinner, or late nights on the weekend. Hope to see you back again soon!

Come hungry.....really hungry. Katz's doesn't do subtle, and neither should you. Ordering at the counter is part of the deal, grab your ticket, don't lose it and step up with confidence. This is New York, after all.  Don't forget to tip your carver! Katz is one of those places you can't get out of my head. Hubby and I did it the only right way: split the corned beef and pastrami Reuben of course with melty cheese, sauerkraut and Russian dressing along with half-sour and half-full pickles and a plate of latkes that were crispy, hot, and straight-up perfect. This is bold, no-nonsense, legendary deli food that doesn't apologize for itself. Big flavors, massive portions and zero pretension. It was the perfect pre-show dinner which made our bellies full and hearts happy.

The best pastrami I've ever had! If I can give this place 10 stars I would! Yes, it is that superb!  The price matches the amount of meat they put in. So thick, juicy, flavorful and tender! We got lucky as we arrived there around 12:20ish and there were about 5 people ahead of us from the outside. Once inside, they give you tickets to take with you in order to place your order at the counters. There are 8 cutter counters that you can order from so be sure to explore shorter counter lines. They will give you samples for the meat if you want to try. Staff are very friendly! They will ask you if you want some fat on your meat, if not they can take it off. The sandwich comes with your choice of sour or non sour pickles. This is the thickest most delicious pastrami sandwich I've ever had. The sandwich is big enough for 2 people. I would be back for sure!

The famous and storied Katz's Deli is exactly the kind of place they advertise. Straight out of the movies, the restaurant is always buzzing with customers, meat cutters and the gentle dance of bus boys cleaning tables the second people get up to make room for more. It really is a surreal experience when you're inside, no directions but you are expected to go up to one of the cutters to get your food and if you want drinks and sides there are other stations for it. Each step the server scribbles a new price on the ticket they give you when entering so that you can pay your bill on the way out. Finding a table, especially for a large group is true adventure. But don't worry you'll find one. As for the food itself, it's large, it's tasty, and it's extremely overpriced. Here you're paying a premium to sit amongst all the photos of the celebrities while you chow down on a sandwich that's really just a bunch of meat on a plate. Come hungry but don't expect to leave completely satisfied because within the glamour there is a small feeling that the magic was mostly for the show and not for the genuine nyc it used to be.

Katz Deli deserves an updated review. I'm giving them Four Stars for delicious homemade style soups, knish, bread, bagels and turkey. Thanks to my Jewish Spiritual Sister and Best Friend for well over 45 years, Shirley. She sent the wellness package for my cancer recovery and birthday in February. My daughter is finally going to help me eat a bagel and some turkey today for lunch. I've been enjoying everything all along as you can see by my photos. The soups are not overly seasoned or salty. They're tasty but very plain. It's great enjoying warm soup in winter. I'm not fond of meat but the turkey is my favorite. I found the carrots under cooked for my liking. If you enjoy going in to the restaurant good for you. Unless it's changed, I hated the set up. I'll just have mine delivered and eat in the comfort of my home. BUT for now, with more bagels in the freezer to eat, I've had enough of Katz eats to last me a YEAR! I'm hankering southern soul cooking!

I don't really see what all the hype is about Katz Deli. We got there early. We didn't wait long to be seated. I just didn't realize it is communal style seating! Our table was against the wall. The table next to us was practically connected to ours. No space in between. They had four guests we were two. It was a mess when we finished our small meal first and needed to get out. It was hard to get the waiters attention. They had to stop eating, get up and move all the chairs to let us pass! I guess since they give you huge portions people think its a great deal. We were hard pressed to find a small version of something. We didn't want to spend so much for food we didn't want to carry home with us. I think we ended up with hot dogs! I was disappointed. I've found Ben's Kosher Deli and Barney Greengrass the Sturgeon King more to my liking. I'll go there instead. If you need to go to say you've been, have fun! That's about all I wanted to do. I think it's noted for being in When Harry Met Sally or some other movie.

Katz is obviously a touristy restaurant, but it lives up to the hype! The line is long but moves relatively fast. Their sandwiches are massive, so either come hungry or with a partner. I've had both their corned beef and pastrami sandwiches before and they were excellent. I ordered the brisket sandwich today and was a little underwhelmed. But I also got the matzo ball soup which was super yummy!! Bring cash if you're in a hurry because the cash line towards the door is usually much short than the card line towards the back of the restaurant. Definitely a good sandwich stop if you have the appetite and extra time!

We're so glad you enjoyed your visit! And though we often serve a full house, if you ever want to try dodging the crowd, drop by at an off-peak hour: breakfast, between lunch and dinner, or late nights on the weekend. Hope to see you back again soon!

WHEN: Wed @7pm Really glad there was no line out there door, but there IS a line at the deli counter inside. They really have a system here: - Every person receives a ticket whether you order or not.  DO NOT LOSE THIS TICKET.  You'll have to surrender it upon exiting. - There are 2 different kinds of counter to order from:  Food (several) and Beverages (one) - If you tip the food counter they will give you a sample to snack on while they make you your sandwich/order. -  After ordering from the food counter, go to the beverage counter if you also want a drink. - Find a place to sit.  It gets so busy you may need to share a table. - Once you are done, you go to another counter to PAY. - Upon exiting, each person is to surrender thier tickets whether they ordered or not, and the receipt (s). I think this is how they make such a high traffic popular place efficient.  Between my partner and I, we ordered: PASTRAMI SANDWICH ON RYE - $28.95 This sandwich came with 2 kinds of pickles and its so fun!  The sandwich itself is so hefty we shared half.  It was rich, flavorful and amazing for something that appears so simple.  It's meat, bread and mustard!  I see the hype there. Yummy! CELERY SODA - $3.95 I don't drink soda.  But I was so curious since I had never come across soda was celery flavored, and it was surprisingly tasty!  It's so subtle, kind of like ordering a cream soda.  It's sweet, it's fizzy, ya can't go wrong! What a lively place this was.  You can easily meet new people here when sharing tables, and they are more than likely to be in a good mood since they are about to have such a yummy sandwich!

Line goes quick to enter the restaurant. System they have is good. Got here around almost 12pm, waiting in line for about five minutes to go in and order. You get a ticket and choose a cutter line to order your sandwich. Ordered the Reuben which is a corned beef pastrami type. It has thousand island dressing on rye and sauerkraut in melted cheese. Look for a seat, ordered the drinks and fries at the other counter. It's crowded but everyone inside is nice knows you just need to be patient. First bite and this is the best. I am not a pastrami type of person but with reviews and everyone saying this place is the best, their logo speaks to itself. It's a big restaurant to accommodate all the customers that come in to try this place. It's a must try and I totally recommend to try if you're NYC.

We're so glad you enjoyed your first visit! And though we do try to keep things moving quickly, if you ever want to try dodging the crowd, drop by at an off-peak hour: breakfast, between lunch and dinner, or late nights on the weekend. Hope to see you back again soon!

First things first: get ready to wait. When we arrived, the line was out the door, down the street, and around the corner. You'll want to make friends with the people around you because you're going to be there a while. Once you finally reach the door, there's a guy controlling the flow, letting in about 30 people at a time. Inside? Absolute chaos--in the best way. You have options: * Stand in line at one of the many counter stations (the counter is long, but there are multiple lines so it moves faster). * Or go to the back and wait again for table service. We chose table service because we were with an elderly uncle who preferred it. From the moment we got in line outside to sitting at a table, it was about 75 minutes. Whew. That's a lot of waiting before even talking about the food. But wow--the food. We all ordered the same thing: the classic pastrami sandwich on rye. We knew it would be massive, so we skipped sides. The matzo ball soup looked incredible, especially since it was freezing outside--next time for sure. We also tried Dr. Brown's cream soda, and they bring a plate of pickles to the table, which pair perfectly with the pastrami. And yes... it really is that good. The pastrami absolutely melts in your mouth. There's a reason this place has lines, and it's not just hype. When you're done, you pay (cash or card) and have to show proof of payment before leaving--which makes total sense given the controlled chaos inside. If you order from the counter, you'll find your own seat. The restaurant is full of large communal tables, so expect to sit with strangers. Honestly, it's part of the experience--get to know your neighbors. Bottom line: it's crowded, loud, and a bit overwhelming, but also iconic, delicious, and genuinely fun. Katz's lives up to the reputation.

Katz's is the most famous restaurant in America. It's been in business for 137 years. Let that sink in for a moment. They've barely changed a thing here. The antiquated ordering system frustrates some people, I find it charming. It's really not that complicated. Find a cutter, stand in line, and order to your heart's content. They give you a sample of pastrami, you watch your creation all carved to order. Pro tip, have a cash tip at the ready for your cutter. I've been eating Katz's for years, as my family always made it a point to visit when we were in New York. And to me, it hasn't lost the excitement. Sure, it's busy. Sometimes there's a line. But there's no pastrami in America that tastes better than Katz's. NONE. If you don't agree, you're simply a curmudgeon. Each sandwich comes with a plethora of pickles. They will cleanse your palette from the rich, fatty, and salty meat. It comes with mustard, but I prefer to douse mine with extra mustard. And a Dr. Brown's cream soda is the icing on the cake. Katz's pastrami sandwich is piled high like no other. If you eat the whole thing you won't be eating for an entire month. You can easily split it with someone, and all of a sudden it's an affordable meal. Legendary. Iconic. An institution. Start spreading the news...Katz's IS New York City. It's "known as the best" for very very good reason. I'm a Katz's lifer. I dream about the pastrami. And I'm counting down the seconds until my next visit!

We came on a Friday before 12 pm and the line moved quick.  By the time we left, the line was tot the end of the block to CVS!  We tried both the Reuben and Pastrami.  We love the Reuben since it had all the dressing.  The celery side tasted similar to ginger ale.  It was a good spot if the line was short.  Not sure if I would wait for 1 hr for it though.

We're so glad you enjoyed your first visit - though we're sorry to hear you were frustrated by the wait! Though we do our best to keep the line moving quickly, if you ever want to try dodging the crowd, drop by at an off-peak hour: breakfast, between lunch and dinner, or late nights on the weekends. Hope to see you back again soon for another Reuben and Cel-Ray fix!

My husband and I came here for the famous sandwich. So good! So much meat. You order at the counter and then pay before you leave. Absolutely crowded inside with a bunch of tables and we went at 11AM on a Sunday.

You can't say you've "done" New York until you've stood in line at Katz's Delicatessen. It's a rite of passage, and even at $40 for a sandwich and tip, it's worth every single penny for the quality and the history. The Main Event: Pastrami on Rye I kept it classic: Pastrami on Rye. No cheese (trust me, you don't need it), just a generous swipe of mustard. * The Meat: Hand-carved, juicy, and melts in your mouth. * The Pairing: The mustard cuts through the richness of the fat perfectly, especially when you alternate bites with their iconic pickles and cucumbers. It's the holy trinity of deli flavors. The Strategy: The "Cutter" Secret Here's an Elite tip for the rookies: If you've been watching their videos on social media and have a favorite cutter, look for their station! You can actually choose which line to stand in. It might sound extra, but the way different cutters slice and portion the meat does make a difference in the texture of the sandwich. The Vibe & Timing I was surprised to find out they are open late--actually 24/7 on weekends. I rolled in around 11:00 PM on a Friday. Even though it didn't look "overly crowded," I still waited about 40 minutes. * Pro Tip: Don't lose your ticket! They give it to you when you walk in, and you must hand it back when you leave, even if it's blank. The Bottom Line: Is it expensive? Yes. Is there a wait? Always. But for the best pastrami on the planet and that chaotic, authentic NYC energy, I'd do it all over again.

Katz's is and will always be a NYC staple! Worth the line that wraps around the block and moves pretty quickly. You receive a ticket upon entering that is used to document what you order. Make sure to hold onto that ticket as that is the only way that the check out employee knows what you ordered. And they can unfortunately fine you for losing it--so guard it carefully. Well, after that stress is over enjoy waiting in line for a little bit as these amazing people gove out fresh roast beef, turkey, pastrami, and other delicious meats. They are generous with their portions and even give you some samples as you wait. They will ask you if you want pickles, take the pickles, and they will ask you what you want on your sandwich--mustard is a must! If you do not get enough mustard they have some on the tables. Now the tables, you have to fight for one, but wait patiently as someone will eventually get up and that is when you swoop in, sit down, and hopefully enjoy your sandwich. All around you are people eating, talking, and enjoying themselves. It is such a good vibe and my mom and I really enjoyed ourselves! Make sure to check out the free water and counters in the back where you can order bagles, bread, potato pancakes, and so many other delicious items!! Do not sleep on Katz and do not let the line stop you. Minus one star as they need to announce that they now take cards and they could have a smoother system for placing orders--especially with our technology!! Thank you Katz for keeping it amazing all these years!

waited for 1 hour to finally get my sandwich. Got the pastrami w cheese and mustard. The whole experience is a true NY experience and would definitely recommend if it's your first time in NY. The sandwich cost 30 dollars and with a beer i spent about 45 dollars total. Honestly it was one of the best sandwiches i've ever had. Perfectly soft rue bread, extremely flavorful pastrami. It wasnt difficult to find a seat even though its packed

Such a good experience! This was some of the best food I had in New York. Their pastrami sandwich was incredible- very tender and seasoned well. My wife and I shared one and it filled us both up. It was $30 but you have to try it at least once.

Quite simply on its own the best pastrami of all time. Pastrami for Pastrami it's the best I have had hands down. The main weakness of Katz is the bread. Although you will be full and have more than enough pastrami for later.

Finally trying out this place after being discouraged by the thousands of people lining up every single day. IT'S OKAY. Nothing special. The best thing here is the MEATS. Tender and absolutely tasty. And they give out LARGE portions on every sandwich. It is the real deal, and no complaints. I have issues with their bread. The rye bread they have break easily and sloppy. Get it with the club bread instead. Also order the combo: pastrami and corn beef. The Reuben is actually good too. THE SAD PART and why it's 3 star rating. The place itself has a very chaotic system of ordering and paying. Note, most of these people are tourists, so they don't know where to start, or where to go when they come in. First, the staff are a little snobbish and sometimes not helpful. When you enter, you get a ticket. Then you go wait for another line for the ordering. There's a different counter for the ordering. And the paying. The paying is on the middle counter. They need a more systematic way of things. This place is loaded with money for every single person that comes in. TOURISTY and PACKED, and chaotic. So prepare yourselves and be kind to yourselves and to other folks. Don't be itchy and unruly while waiting.

We're glad you enjoyed your meal, but so sorry to hear that you had a negative service experience - we never want any of our customers to feel exasperated by the ticket process! Though part of our charm for many of our customers is our "old-school New York" attitude, including our system of payment, we understand that the atmosphere is not for everybody. It's never meant to be rude, just schtick - that being said, the treatment that you received should never be the case. We will take your experience to heart - please feel free to call and speak to a manager anytime!

We were in NYC for a holiday weekend between Hanukkah, Christmas and New Years. Our son required us to go to Katz's Deli for an authentic Jewish deli experience and food! It was  an incredible experience dining at the spectacular & iconic Katz's Delicatessen @katzsdeli in New York City to celebrate the start of a New Year of 2026. Founded in 1888 this historic deli is 2nd to none! From its wait team including our kind, funny and dry humor Ismael who was excellent taking our order, service and a few items "to go" including a loaf of Jewish rye bread, huge beef salami, bagels, babka, a Katz's Deli cap and T-shirt. We order the latkes, with apple sauce a d sour cream, pastrami on rye, a turkey Ruben and soup and sandwich combo. It was our selections were ALL huge and delicious and was beyond expectations for our son and worth the 30 minutes wait in the 30 degrees. The restaurant is 1940's retro which seems to be a "time capsule" for mid century as well the movie scene from director Rob Reiner's classic Rom Com "When Harry Met Sally"  staring Meg Ryan and Bill Crystal from 1989. The famous lines Meg orgasmic screamed and Reiner's own mother stated "I'll Have Whats She's Having!" Will forever live in these walls. Hundreds of "Wall of Stars" as on the restaurant including Danny DeVito, Tom Selleck, Serene Williams, Mike Myers (Austin Powers) and some many more. Thanks Ismael for making our son Jacob's first visit to Katz's Deli memorable and special! It's an experience & meal we will cherish for its uniqueness, freshness & quality of food, prompt & excellent service, kind hospitality and its authenticity. Bravo! Encore! #katzsdeli #jewishdeli #nyc #minionhousesf

Best pastrami in the world, period. Service is excellent, meat is carved in front of your eyes and you get to taste the meat before receiving your sandwich. Plenty of seating inside with clean restrooms, fun to see all the memorabilia on the walls that have accumulated over the last few decades.

A very popular tourist stop, Katz's deli is worth the visit for both the food and the experience. This location, on Houston St, is not next to any other tourist attraction so if you're coming out this way, you're going to Katz's. There sometimes is a line to get in that stretches down the block but it moves pretty quickly. Once in the door, you'll receive a ticket and head to the counter. There are multiple stations at the counter; head towards any of the meat slicer guys and order what you want. Drinks are another line and credit card pay is at the very end. Your ticket will get marked with what you ordered and you pay on the eay out. Find seating where you can. OR, if you head towards the red door on the back wall and take a right, you'll be at the waiting area for the table service section, waiter and all. The pastrami is the obvious standout and it delivers. Flavorful, soft, and plentiful. The pastrami sandwich should be shared and is huge. Add a side of fries, matzo ball soup, or pickles and you'll be set.

We're so glad to hear you enjoyed your visit! And yes - though we do often serve a full house, we try to keep things moving quickly. If you ever want to try dodging the crowds though, drop by at an off-peak hour: breakfast, between lunch and dinner, or late nights on the weekends. Hope to see you back again soon for another pastrami fix!

ONE MUST GO HERE IF IN NY! You're cheating yourself out of a culinary explosion  if not! BEST PASTRAMI I've ever had.  And I've had enough to say I'm almost an expert  it's tender juicy and they load up the sandwich on a really mild rye (I typically don't favor rye) you can add cheese etc but I would suggest you keep it simple with a little mustard and savor the flavor! I'm sure it's more mild on weekdays but we went on a Saturday and the line was around the corner but better than I thought we had made it inside in about 40 mins or so - they have a system - you either get in the line to place your order and grab a table where found or they have table service and since we were party of two we only had about 10-15 mins before seated.   They use a ticket system - you pay after eating - if paying cash up front paying with card at the back and you have to keep the receipt to exit the store! It's a typical Jewish Deli - loud but welcoming and seems like total confusion but their system works. The latkes are the bomb.com also - huge and very flavorful with lots of potatoes n onions and nicely seasoned served with traditional sour cream and applesauce! The cukes are good too - one is more like a cucumber with a slight garlic nod and the other is the traditional deli super sour n garlicky pickle! They ship so I might order some pastrami and have it at home It was fun looking at all the pics of local and national celebrities that have visited.

First time back in almost a decade, and tasted even better than before! Got the Reuben with pastrami and potato salad. 10/10 for both. Great acidity on the potatoes, the sandwich is fantastic. Tried the regular pastrami last time with just mustard and that was good, you get sauerkraut and melted cheese on the Reuben.
Classics stay classic for a reason. So glad you enjoyed your return visit - hopefully round three comes a little sooner!

A tourist trap restaurant for sure, but when asking locals if there is a better option than Katz for Deli sandwiches as good as Katz, I didn't get an answer . Until I find that restaurant for cheaper, Katz gets a 5/5. Also, the sandwich was so so good ‍. I will say when I went on a Monday night, it was not busy. Of course, make sure to bring cash and tip for samples.

I could do not in this place was so good and worth the wait even if it was a long... this is also the spot where they filmed Billy Crystal and Meg Ryan movie directed by Rob Reiner (rest in peace), When Harry Met Sally. We waited a bit to get an order in but worth the wait. The beef is so tender and you don't need a lot of condiments on the sandwich just a little bit of mustard and what not and a side of pickle and you're good to go. That thing was flavored up and the pickles were a little salted, but that's also well balanced for when you're switching between the sandwich and the matzo soup. Tastes like chicken noodle soup you keep forgetting you're eating bread ball though. I would love to try the other dishes. They have there as there's more options than just the sandwich. Gotta make my way from Portland again to come here.

A NY classic establishment that is exactly what you'd expect it to be if you're expecting large portions, delicious food, quick service and a lot of other patrons. I came by for an early lunch around 11a on a Monday--I'd encourage you to do the same to avoid the 12p lunch lines which were out the door. You can grab a random seat/table or wait for a server in the back. I went with the former option which I think works well for parties of 1-4 people. I split the traditional pastrami, latkes and knish and had waaaaay too much food for two. Looking back, I'd skip the latkes next time (but that's just because my stomach was full). Get yourself to this classic spot!

Shake Shack is a NY staple, so of course you'll find it at the Citifield Stadium. This is also one of the largest vendors for food here as there are 3 sets of lines to order from. They have all the burgers lined up in the kitchen, so it makes it quick and easy to grab and go once you order. We got our food within a few minutes of paying and back to our seats. We ordered the Shack Stack ($14.59), Chicken Stack ($10.19), Double Shackburger ($11.49), Hot Dog ($5.19), and Cheese Fries ($7.49). Note the prices are slightly higher than outside the stadium, but that's how baseball games are. The Shack Stack is tasty and I also love the cheesiness from the fried shroom. I'd pass on the chicken stack though, as their burgers are the best items here. The quality is the same and great to enjoy while watching the game.

I was pleasantly surprised by the stadium food. The shake shack here had multiple lines and I would say they moved pretty fast. The staff was friendly and fast, which I wasn't expecting since the stadium was packed. I got the fries and a chicken burger. I did think $9 for a small side of fries was ridiculous, but needless to say, they were not greasy at all and perfectly crispy so I was happy. My change chicken burger was decent. The flavor was good as was the aiole on it, but I found myself having to take pieces of the breading of the chicken out of my mouth because there were pieces that were too hard that I couldn't chew. Nonetheless, pretty good for stadium good.

I can't believe I am writing this, but I have come to appreciate the consistency of this Shake Shack. It does what it does and it don't what it don't.  Ball park prices aside, consistency has it's merits.

My recent visit to Shake Shack was filled with both delightful surprises and ordinary experiences. The cornerstone of any burger joint, the burger itself, was undeniably fantastic. It truly lived up to Shake Shack's reputation. The beef patty was cooked to perfection: juicy, flavorful, and with just the right amount of char. It was complemented well by the fresh lettuce, tomato, and a bun that held its own without stealing the show. As for the fries, they were fair but lacked that unique "wow" factor. They were crisp and decently seasoned, yet they didn't quite match the excellence of the burger. If they upped their fries game to match their burgers, Shake Shack could truly become an unbeatable combination. Overall, I'd recommend Shake Shack for their burgers anytime. It's a four-star experience that could easily become five with just a little more attention to the side dishes. Can't wait to return and see what other burger magic they have in store! Service was great! Really nice workers

I like shake shack, we recently got one in Oregon! We ate at the one at Citi Field and it was good and service great. Loved the area it was in too, we did a pregame tour and had a good amount of time to kill before the game so we were able to come here and eat and then go shop at the team store. Shake shack was great and I learned that the original started in Central Park as a food cart and now they are clear in Oregon and delicious! I love the burgers and fries.

extremely disappointed by the expensive burgers I got yesterday At  Citifield.  I was embarrassed I bought my granddaughter there for burgers.  i neglected to look at them and went back to our seats.  The burgers were burnt and my granddaughter did not eat hers. I broke off the outside of the burnt burger and ate it because it was expensive and it was far from our seats to go back.  So disappointed in the condition of the burgers they SHOULD NOT HAVE BEEN SERVED to anyone that burnt.  check out your food before you leave here.

Ordered a milkshake at shake shack, cashier proceeded to get pissed at me and served me a shake that was not spun at all and was full of ice chunks and the ice cream was stuck to the bottom. Total rip off especially after paying the stadium up charge.

Not too crazy, it was actually pretty quick to come in and order a shake, beer, rosé wine and of course their burgers. They even have a breakfast menu here that looks appealing with coffees.  There's some seating and everything looks bright, new and clean.

One of the best food options in Citi Field. If you're jonesing for an amazing burger, stay far away from the regular ball park burgers and get Shake Shack. The quality is vastly different. Same goes for the fries.

The line is always so extremely long that I miss multiple innings because of it, but I decided to take a chance during a recent Mets game. Only missed 2 innings at the beginning of the game, but it was definitely worth it. There's something about eating Shake Shack at the best baseball stadium (long-suffering Mets fan here) and enjoying a beautiful night of baseball (despite another Mets loss). Overall, this Shake Shack didn't disappoint -- just be prepared to wait on line for a long time. As long as you have good company and pay attention to the game on the TV while waiting, you should be good to go!

While the burger and fries are what you expect from Shake Shack(decent fast food), this Citi Field location was overpriced with less than stellar customer service. In addition to our food we had ordered two sodas and and Smartwater for later. When we got the Smartwater, they had taken the cap off of the drink as per "policy". So now we had to carry it back to our seets, spilling half on the way. Later, we discovered that other food outlets were selling water with the caps on. This was annoying. Also, the guy who rang us up had his mask pulled down over his chin and he spit when he talked. Gross. Luckily, he wasn't assembling our order. In summary, go to one of the other food outlets if you're at Citi Field. You can always hit up Shake Shack at another location.

Hi Shane, Thank you for your feedback. It's disappointing to read that your experience at the Shack wasn't up to our standards. It sounds like we dropped the ball at several points during your visit. We can do better than what you experienced, so we'd love to invite you back to the Shack. Could you message me with your email so that we can grab your details? Thank you again, Jake

Shake shack in name only....watered down lemonade, crappy burger ,no pickles, no chicken tenders, and folks have an attitude......shame, was here before pandemic and recollect it being good....do yourself a favor, just get a hot dog....Go Mets.

I FORGOT HOW GOOD SHAKE SHACK'S SALTY FRIES ARE!! i'm so glad i had them to keep me company through this met's game!! not to mention I also tried their BLACK & WHITE SHAKE.. mMMmm not too thick or sweet!! the fries & shakes trump California's In n Out, but In n Out's still got the upper hand on standard burgers unfortunately they don't offer the "shack stack" at this location so i skipped on the burgers! NOTE: baseball stadium food is usually way over priced BUT i felt like shake shack kept their prices within an reasonable range! the line can be ridiculous, but if you go on an off day like i did.. NO WAIT

Always good food! I normally always end up here if I am at a Mets game! The food is good and the line usually moves quick. The burgers are juicy and cooked well. The shroom burger is also really good! I ordered it by accident once but I ended up really enjoying it! The fries are tasty. Great food for a baseball game! My favorites: Single ShackBurger with cheese, 'Shroom Burger and Fries

OMG...  Please don't tell mew that you have never had a Shake Shack burger...   Please!  This incredibly tasty piece of meat with cheese on their signature bun is nothing less than awesome. It's all about the taste, and a Shake Shack burger comes with plenty of it.  Even they're "shroom' burger was a tasty fried breaded mushroom with cheese on the same signature bun, or as their menu says: Crisp-fried portobello mushroom filled with melted muenster and cheddar cheeses, topped with lettuce, tomato, ShackSauce™."  It was awesome. Don't let the crazy long line at Citi Field deter you.  Every time I have been on it I have moved quickly through the maze to the counter.  The team members are always smiling and friendly and I can not imagine the pressure that they go through. I one mouth a burger at the 8th inning simply because there were only three people on line and did not want to pass on the opportunity.  We tried something new this time...  "The Concrete."  This vanilla custard in a cup is made with chocolate sprinkles and a cone all blended together, a new level of good!

Food: As usual, the best burger in NYC with the longest line ever. I would suggest if you are willing to wait on this line order more then you want so you have no regrets when the burger is all gone in your tummy lol. I recommend to go for the shake burger double and one of their flat top hot dogs. This will get your through the game with no regrets. Brew: There's not much of a selection here since it's a ball park but they do have something very special to pick over your water down lite garbage beer, Goose Island IPA. It's $10.50 for a 16 oz can but its delicious, cold, and the best beer pick to enjoy your time there.

My first Mets game and being hungover as all get out of town, I decided to opt for having Shake Shack. Something I don't normally splurge on. Others went for fish and chips. Yeah. . . . if I'm forking over $10-15 on stadium food, you may as well go big or go home. By the sixth inning the line wasn't too horrible. It moved pretty fast. The prices are a bit skewed from the normal locations in the city. Normally a single burger is like $5-6, here it was about $7.50. Normally a double is roughly $8, here it was about $10.50. After deliberating some time I finally decided since I never had it, I wanted to try the shroom burger, but I also didn't want to be healthy and opted for the Shack Stack: A shroom burger on top of a regular burger. Was it worth it? Yes, hell yes. The shroom burger may bizarrely actually taste better to me than the regular. The regular I feel like you can slide american cheese on it from anywhere and have it taste like any generic fast food cheeseburger. This heaping breaded sucker was oozing with both muenster and cheddar cheese and quite flavorful. The special shack sauce (some ketchup mayo hybrid innovation of shear delight) sealed the deal and that extra kick of bovine on the end - perfection. This was actually worth $10.50. The concrete thing . . . . I've never had one and I have heard so many raving comments and reviews on their frozen custard. . . . so boring and disappointing. A waste of precious calories. The Mets stadium has a special called 'The Strike Cone': Vanilla frozen custard, blended with chocolate truffle cookie dough, shattered sugar cone, and chocolate sprinkles. I'm betting that Shake Shack unfortunately ran out of nearly all of their ingredients though because the only thing in this was chocolate sprinkles. A huge disappointment leading to children everywhere sobbing into their frozen custards over the lack-thereof of cookie dough and anything truffle. My first time was tarnished, but it doesn't mean I won't ever go to a Shake Shack again. I will just be more apprehensive on my order.

I missed two innings of the Mets vs. Twins game on June 25th as I stood in line for my S-squared fix. Ladies and gentlemen, it was well worth it. I haven't had Shake Shack since last summer at their Madison Park location, so I was due for a single shack burger and its accompanying sauce of excellence. Oh yes, and a side of frozen custard to boot. The line coils around like a slithery snake, but it moves at a tolerable pace so you don't get too impatient and/or anxious. The mega-screen of the live game provides reasonable justification to wait in line as your seat gets cold. My burger was warm and juicy, and nicely charred and that shack sauce should definitely be bottled and sold. The frozen custard is devilishly good as well, reminiscent of Mister Softee ice cream, albeit a bit thicker in texture. To be honest, I may have been more stoked over Shake Shack than seeing my beloved Mets play in their new (gorgeous and fan-friendly) stadium. That being said, Let's Go Mets! We beat the Twins 5-2 that night. Holler!!

No... Just... No. What are you people thinking?  Just because you may like one Shake Shack burger does not mean you must love them all!  A grease pocket with overcooked flavorless beef. If the original Shake is as bad as this, I am not surprised to see it tumble down the list of 'top burgers' in the city.  Small, no ability to vary, no pickles even! Thank heavens I had just had a very good burger at Bonfire Grill in Forest Hills a day or so before, or I would be even sadder at this culinary fiasco. And having just eaten at The Modern last week -  I think Mr Meyer really needs to REthink his investment or attention to Shake Shack.  Burger fans deserve better, Danny boy!

I truly dont get the Shake Shack obsession, I think it just shows how the media can sway peoples opinions because I honestly think Shake Shack is awful. Not just this one but all of them. Burger is greasy,sauce is cloying and roll is nothing special. The burgers are so bad they nearly killed Met first basemen  Lucas Duda and Phillies manager Ryne Sandberg. What causes my insane hatred for this particular outlet is that people buy tickets for a baseball game and then spend 2-3 inning waiting on a line for an over hyped burger when they can get a burger at Pat lafriedas or Keiths Grill. Better yet get some BBQ from Blue Smoke (I dont have a Danny Meyer hate just a Shake Shack hate) if you just want to eat Shake Shack go to one of the many other ones! Ok my rant is over.
What used to be good fast food is now crappy fast food. The burgers and hot dogs are small and the fries are really bland. And the line is really long; not worth the wait.

You can't go wrong! I guess since the shacks are limited in locations this one BOOMs. People that get to the games 2 hours early get the cream of the crop. Everyone else can stand in line for two hours for a try. The burgers are tasty and made well done no matter what. Everything is a la carte so you have to order sides. The milk shakes are thick and delicious. Deff a good try if you get there early!

Standing on the "Green Roof" of CitiField, after a long and somewhat boring CLE course, I looked down at the Shake Shack line and thought to myself, "look at all those assholes standing there for burgers."  An hour later, I added myself to that list; waiting in line from the bottom of the first until the end of the third inning...the whole time, sweating like a whore in church! The Shake Shack burgers and fries are just as good as they are at Madison Square Park, the only difference is I paid a $50 buck surcharge for this one.  I'm a Yankee fan anyway, but I suppose if I went to another Mets game, I'd probably wait on that long ass line again.

This location is inside of Citi Field, and I love the decor of it.  The line gets really LOONNNNGGGGG though, but it is well worth the wait.  Just know what you're going to order when you get up there and everything will be OK.  Also, not sure if it's just me but the prices seem higher here.  Moving on ... I haven't gotten anything from Shake Shack that I didn't love, which leads me to believe that you just can't go wrong here.  I love their Shake Stack, cheese fries, with a strawberry shake ... but since I'm not always that hungry I'll switch around my order a bit.  But I will always get an extra side or two of their shake sauce ... Yumm!! If Shake Shack is ever an option ... then that will always be my first choice -- just in case you haven't noticed that by now ;).

Citi Field Shake Shack is just as good as any other Shake Shack in New York City. I got a single shack, French fries, and vanilla shake. The burger was cooked perfectly just the way I like it. The cheese was just oozing when you bite into it. I was in heaven. Best burger in the world. My French fries just perfect. Shake shack fries are always cooked to perfection. It wasn't soggy at all. Yummy!!! My vanilla shake was amazing. Right off the blender. Score!!! I would suggest getting shake shack before the game when the lines are not crazy. During the game the lines will get insanely crazy. You may be online for quite a while, so you have been warned. The person who took my order, Brian C. Was really quick with orders and really friendly. Its located behind center field on the field level. Its the only Shake Shack stand in the stadium. Citi Field Shake Shack is one the best foods to eat in citi field.

The Mets game is the price you pay to gain admission to the glory that is Shake Shack. It's technically the Shake Shack in the city with the most seating. You have more than half a stadium of seats to choose from (since no one cares where you sit anymore). I suggest buying more than what you think you can eat to last you the whole depressing game. *Also, please note that there's an evil exhaust vent that blows the smell of onions and meaty goodness all over the stadium throughout the game. So if you're all out of Shack by then, you'll want to murder someone because you were dumb enough to buy only one burger, and have to either brave the Shack line again, or sit through the remainder of the game being assaulted by the smell of heavenly grease. (in a good way)

First time in Citifield yesterday and I had a chance to get some Shake Shack.  What more can you ask for in a Mets game?  Well it would have been nice if they won.  But I also went on free t-shirt day so I guess that balances it out.  :p FYI the fry stand across from Shake Shack has pretty good fries with some interesting sauces.  I said interesting I didn't say amazing.

This is a review for the food.   Since I had $30 in Citi Field credit to use, I decided to blow ALL of it or at least most of it at the Shake Shack.  I was at Citi Field the previous night for a game and the line during the game was too long.  So my strategy was to wait and use all my credit and get to the park early to avoid the line.  I ended up getting the double Shackburger, the High Heat Cheese Dog, and the Meet the Pretz concrete shake.  Total: over 2200 calories in one meal and $25 of my credits. The burger was just okay.  It was cooked well and the meat was juicy but it just tasted so...unhealthy.  You might be saying...duh...you're eating a burger.  Perhaps it's my In N Out burger biased but I think whatever oil they used to cook the burgers with was way greasier than I preferred.  The hot dog was pretty decent.  It came with a cheese sauce and moderately spicy cherry peppers on top.  I ate that roughly midway through the game as the burger really did a number on me.  Lastly, I slowly sipped the chocolate covered pretzel shake with black and white custard inside.  This whole meal was challenging that I was going between diabetic coma from the concrete versus almost heart attack inducing greasy meal from the burger and hot dog.  BUT, I made it through and I can now honestly say that I truly had a taste of the Shake Shack during my stay in NY. I think the concrete and the hot dog that I got was only available at the Citi Field Shake Shack which is awesome.  I definitely want to try something else at another more standardized Shake Shack location.

Hey! It's just like an actual Shake Shack but with longer lines and a staff that isn't as well trained! I waited half an inning for my burger while I just stood at the line looking like I was the counter's high school buddy who wanted to chat. I don't know why it took so long for my single to cook up but it did and got no apology or explanation.

HOLY SHNIKIES!!! I think I died and went to heaven. Visiting Shake Shack was on the list of things to do while in NY, and I'm sure glad I did. I am an In-N-Out lover but this place sure does give it a run for it's money. Ordered two double cheeseburgers, order of fries with cheese sauce to share, and a small soda. Everything was delicious. The burgers are simple; topped with lettuce, tomato and shake sauce. Yum. Too bad there isn't one closer to me. Watched a little of the game and went back to try the frozen custard in a cup with strawberries. It was great. Only downside, everything is pretty expensive and they don't offer any type of combo meals.

Tried Shake Shack for the first time after all the hype, and their burger was perfect. Man if the line wasn't as long I would have gone back for seconds or thirds. Missed a lot of the Mets game because of waiting on line for 45 minutes, but it was damn well worth it!

Pros: Compared to everything else at Citi Field, Shake Shack is the same price, if not cheaper. beer served at SS counter Cons: Price may be the same, but lines are longer burger doesn't taste like a SS burger, but decent burger: $6.25 hot Dog: $5.75 large beer: $7.50 cheese Fries: $6
Worth the wait? Yes. Worth the price? No. Would we go again? Probably, because the food and shakes are really good. Probably the best food stand at the stadium.

Truly one of the best locations you can place a cult-like following chain fast food restaurant. Shake Shack serves one of the best burgers you will ever taste from a fast food joint! On just about all occasions before and during the game, the line is usually redunkalous and can range from anywhere from 30-45 minutes! With all that said, the burgers are well worth it! The recommended burger of choice is undoubtedly the Shack Stack! It's a cheeseburger and shroom burger topped with lettuce, tomato and Shacksauce. Did I mention it's huge!? Although not the equivalent to the Animal Style burgers at In N Out, it more than holds its own for the east coast. The crinkle fries are decent, however not the best I've ever tasted. I do recommend getting the cheese fries though if you are going to get the fries. My beverage of choice is usually the Strawberry shake which alot of people rave about. I actually don't think it's that great of a shake for $5. I think that McD's shakes are actually better! Yes I said it! Also, I've gone to other restaurants and burger restaurants which serve much better shakes. In closing, it's worth the money, but maybe not worth the wait at times due to all the options at Citi Field. There's plenty of other Shake Shacks in NYC that you can go to another time, but if you feel the need for your Shake Shack fix then you gotta go get it hereI guess :)

I'm not ashamed to admit that I was looking forward to Shake Shack more than the Mets vs. Padres game.  This has to be the most popular vendor at the game, nestled towards the back of the stadium (behind the scoreboard), with two separate long lines to order your burger, fries, hot dog, or shake. We opted for the single burger, which was on the smaller side but quite flavorful.  The fries more than enough to share. There's not much more to say other than what's already been said -- the meat is incredibly fresh; the fries were nothing special. Of the top burger places in the nation, this is how I'd rank them: 1. In-N-Out Burger 2. Shake Shack 3. Five Guys If you're heading to the beautiful Citi Field, definitely grab a bite at Shake Shack.  It's pricey, but what isn't in a ballpark?

If you can stand waiting in line for almost 3 innings of the game you will be rewarded with some of the best food around. The burger is perfectly cooked and juicy the way ti should be. The cheese fries are absolute perfection. A single shack burger with cheese fries and a aquafina water will set you back $17 but it's well worth it

Worst Nightmare: went there during the game on 7/7/22 against the Marlins. Stood on line for literally a half an hour just to place an order. The cashiers were slow and had their backs turned to chat with other staff members. After placing our orders, we waited again for over a half an hour just to get our food and it was wrong. We asked for 2 hamburgers with no cheese and not sauce, the first time they made it with no cheese but heavy on the sauce, then they made it again with no sauce but had cheese on it. How incompetent can they be? We missed 3 innings of the game thanks so such ignorance and incompetence. The entire staff needs to be fired immediately!
A delightful treat  upon the pallet, but seriously if you haven't tried shake whack you're just wasting your time. Add bacons, double the patties and skip the tomato.

Went to the one in Manhattan about three years ago, and I wanted to try it again. Wanted a good burger, and was told that Shake Shack was the way to go. I walked out to left field, and this is the most popular concession stand at Citi Field. I must have waited a good 10 minutes in line, but the line was moving. Once you got up there, I had the Shake Stack and Cheese Fries and it was really good, the burger and the portobello mushroom together with the sauce was great. Also ordered cheese fries and they were really good.

Hamburgers. The cornerstone to any nutritious breakfast. And it was my breakfast when we saw the SF Giants play the Brooklyn Cyclones....err, I mean the NY Mets last Sunday. Lining up, for a second I thought I was at Madison Square Park because the line was about 40 people deep. But then I looked around, saw all the signs for Budweiser, EA Sports, Blue Smoke and no NY Mets pictures whatsoever, and I knew I was at CitiField. The good thing is that the line moves pretty fast, so we were on line for about 15 minutes. Of course I had to get a Double Shack burger and fries. But because of a minor physical defect, I couldn't get a black & white shake and had to settle for a Mountain Dew, which  hit the spot anyway. The burger was just as good as the burger at Madison Square Park, even if it was already made. That's the thing I like about this Shake Shack: you will get your food within a minute or two of ordering. Unlike Madison Square Park, where you have to wait almost as long as you did before you ordered. Only bad thing: the Mets won on a walk-off single in the bottom of the ninth.
One of the great staples of citi field.  Line could get long.. but that doesn't matter because no one goes to Mets games anymore lol

If you're inside CitiField, definitely head over to the Shake Shack for some burgers and fries. I was willing to wait, in the rain, for fifteen minutes, for: 4 single shack burgers 1 Shackago dog 2 large Pepsi's 1 black and white frozen custard 2 fries No, I'm not that much of a pig. This was for me and my family. How long did it take to get all of them? Five minutes. I'm in awe. As always, their shackburgers were great, and their French fries are excellent. I usually like to slather on ketchup or hot sauce with my fries, but these actually tasted better without them. The Shackago dog was forgettable. Sadly, I have to drop one star because my beloved 'shroom burger is alas, not present (understandably so, but still!). All in all, a great place to get food. The line is not as epically slow as the one in Madison Sq. Park, they're faster (even if pre-made, but beggars can't be choosers), and you get to watch a Mets game. Plus, the prices are actually not exorbitant, which is... a plus.

I have to admit, going to Shake Shack was our top priority of our Mets game experience.  Definitely not the BEST but pretty damn good burgers, great fries and AWESOME shakes.  It's sad the I worked across from the Shake Shake in Madison Square Park for 9 months and this is the first time I had em.  It did NOT disappoint!  I guess we were lucky, we got through the line in about 10 minutes! We got burgers, fries (nice and crispy) and a vanilla shake.  I was definitely between a 3-4 starts but that shake gave this place a solid 4!

I can't believe that my first visit ever to a Shake Shack was at Citi Field...and didn't suck!! Yes, it was even worth waiting on that crazy long line for TWO INNINGS!! How fresh could a shake, burger and fries be at a sporting event? SO FRESH..that's why you're waiting forever for it! I actually saw them making the shakes the old fashioned way behind the counter...really pleased to see this! The burger was delicious..definitely not wimpy. I was worried that the fries would be a disaster but they were crispy and addictive! I'm a fan!

Its a Shake Shack at Citi field what could go wrong? Well other then the insane lines not much. Its the same great Shake Shack. The prices aren't even that bad for ballpark food, such a nice change to paying $8 for a crappy burger at Shea. Pro Tip: If you think waiting in the long lines will save you from watching the Mets loose your out of luck, they have some nice big screens you can watch the game on while waiting in line.

I have been told for years to try Shake Shack. Only problem was, originally there was just the one down in Madison Square Park, an area I rarely end up in.  Then one opened on 77th & Columbus, just after I left my voice teacher, who lives on that block .... so that wasn't an option either. Enter my friend Richard, a dedicated Mets fan, who has tried to get me to a Mets game for some years now.  He finally succeeded, and I am really happy I went - it was a great evening, even if the team lost. However, we started the evening off with burgers from the Shake Shack there.  Good thing we got to the stadium EARLY.  Later on the lines were pretty scary!!  These burgers truly are some of the best I've tried (although Nolita House still holds top spot for now).  I found myself taking tiny bites to make it last longer.  The B&W shake was quite good as well....but we opted for fries across the way (which I was not so impressed with). If you're headed to a Mets game, do NOT miss those burgers!!

It was a semi-rainy weeknight and towards the end of the regular season. You would think that there's no line for this place. NOT! When we walked by to head to our seats, there was no line. But when my friend went to get our burgers, he said there was a wait. =! The single shack burger was perfect. Indeed, it isn't a very big burger but juicy it was and it hit the spot. The fries were ok. The shake, now, that was good! Went with the strawberry shake and yep, it was worth losing that calorie counter gadget for this one night.  Definitely a notch up compared to the other fast food burger joints.

I had a fantastic time seeing the Mets beat the Marlins this past week. Citi Field was fairly clean and very accommodating with food and drink selection. The prices of nearly everything seemed absolutely insane, but the Shake Shack was much more reasonable, as was the pizza spot. The pizza was pretty solid, sporting a fantastic sauce and good cheese. The crust, however, was burned to a crisp in most spots which really killed the flavor towards the end. The smoke shack burger from Shake Shack was absolutely fantastic. Fresh ingredients and a great combination of spice and cheese really made the burger stand out.  The french fries were also pleasantly crispy and delicious. The vanilla milkshake was high quality with a great frothy consistency and a rich creamy vanilla taste.

I'm so sorry but i have been to a few shake shacks and they all have been great but this shake shack let me down so bad . bad enough the wait was super long and you missed a few innings at the game my burger was super salty and so flat and so burnt it was not a shake shack burger to me. i don't think i be hitting up shake shack at citified in a long time i was SO disappointed . maybe next time i  will have a better experience

Being a diehard, loyal Mets fan since I could remember, it pains me to say that the best part of watching a game at Citi Field during this lost season was visiting the popular restaurant beyond the seats in left-center field: Shake Shack. I know this isn't a sports review site, but lemme just say that the Mets really let me down this year. *Sigh* Ok, now that I wiped those tears away, I feel better now. Anyways, I can't state anything here that hasn't been said before. So let me just reiterate all the "yummy goodness" that my wife experienced when she ate here for the first time. My wife is a food-fanatic, an undercover food critic herself when we eat out at a new place. So I hope I can accurately recall all the details she mumbled that day with her mouth full after each bite of food, and slurp of drink. "The burger meat here is so tender and juicy, almost like they marinated it in butter when they cooked it! The hamburger bun is just the perfect size, and doesn't take away from the taste of what's inside. I love the Shack Sauce on it, whatever that is. Heck, the smell of the burger alone makes it better than other burgers!" Yes, it is a lil pricey, but that didn't stop us from eating two double-burgers each!! We tried the Shack-Cago Hotdog also, but it wasn't worth the money. To us, it's just your garden-variety hotdog. We've never been to the other Shake Shack spots, but we can definitely say the burgers we ate were delicioso. We give the burgers a rating of 7... on a 1-5 scale! Whaaat!! So do yourselves a favor, and try the burgers. You can thank us later. And tell 'em Marcus (and wife) sent ya... ;p

Pricey but delicious! I've been to Citi Field numerous of times but only tried Shake Shack twice because the line always looks so long. Although the line may be long, it moves rather fast. We only missed half of an inning waiting which isn't too bad. I ordered two single Shack Burgers, fries, and a black & white shake. Thee shack sauce in the Shack burger was friggin good! Served on a soft warm bun with gooey melted cheese along with a juicy beef patty. Pretty tasty for a burger priced at $7.50. It's a bit small but this is by far the best thing I've eaten so  far at a ballpark. The wavy fries are nice and crispy. No sogginess whatsoever. The shake was great! You can taste bits and chunks of ice cream. Verdict - I could see why the line is always so long now. It's just that darn good. There's never a line at Blue Smoke or the Pizza joint. When you're looking for something to eat at Citi Field, you're gonna wanna come to Shake Shack!

One of the good things about Citi Field is the great concessions they have.. and Shake Shack is prob their best! Yes, the lines are long and you sometimes have to wait 2-3 innings but c'mon, it's Shake Shack.. lines are always long! The menu at their Citi Field location is less varied and the custard flavors are more limited than their other locations but the quality and consistency of the food is the same. Prices are a tad higher but are pretty reasonable considering you expect to pay ballpark prices.. $6.25 for a single and $9.25 for a double vs $5.75 and $8.75 at their other locations. Tips: -Get on line as soon as you get to the ballpark. -There are 2 lines; the one on the right moves quicker since it is serviced by 1 extra register.

You know I used to love shake shack ever since they opened, but I feel like their meat quality has gone down. Last time I came here with my parents the meat tasted completely different and I didn't even finish my burger. Fries are really good, but burger, i dont know it has changed. Not a fan anymore, I rather get chick fil-a.

Hi Andrea, Thank you for your feedback. It's disappointing to read that your meal wasn't up to our standards, since we pride ourselves on the quality of our food. We can do better than what you've experienced, so we'd love to invite you back to the Shack. Could you message me with your email so that we can grab more details? Thank you again, Jake

I must admit that I don't hit burger joints real frequently.  Most common is the staple run through In-N-Out in AZ.  Grabbed Shake Shack at recommendation of our hosts in NY and was STUNNED.  No need to compare the two.  If you've lived in NY all your life and never experienced In-N-Out....you ain't missing anything. I love In-N-Out but Shake Shack dominates in 3 rather key areas (Burgers, Shakes and Fries).  Outstanding.  We are heading back tomorrow and although I want to try the Pulled Pork at Blue Smoke I don't know that I will forgive myself for skipping out on these burgers.  Huge fans.  Can't wait till the game tomorrow......

Danny Meyer truly brings his food to the masses at Citi Field! The menu is a little more expensive and more limited (more limited on the shakes, drinks, no chicken brats and none of the veggie burgers that even carnivores crave), but I think they've done a good job of maintaining the quality of the food here. The line can be daunting, especially before the game, but I found that they move it along well. During the middle innings, the wait was about 15-20 minutes, about double what you'd normally wait at the ballpark, but not that bad overall, especially considering that the wait in Madison Square Park can be epic. A definite must if you have outfield seats.

Color me impressed. I didn't have high expectations for a limited-menu satellite location of Shake Shack in a ball field, but these guys do deliver. We waited in line for about an inning and a half (or two), but when we got our meal it was fresh and delicious. Not world changing, but up there with Five Guys or Elevation Burger - aka the best fast food burgers you can get, IMHO. The shakes and fries are also delicious too, I was surprised to see them scooping ice cream into metal shake containers and running them in a old diner-style blender at with the huge lines they serve, but I guess that's how they maintain quality. Cheese fries were delicious and SUPER filling, too. I'd go again. The shack stack was pretty cool too, I liked not having to decide which of their burgers to get, haha.

Let me begin by saying I... am a hardcore Yankee fan! Now that that's out there, I was recently given tickets for the Delta Club at Citi Field. The seats were great. Fourth row, center field. As good as it gets. But the best part of this entire experience was...... THE SHAKE SHACK  BURGER! WHOA, it blew my mind. SOOOOO much more than I ever expected. The sauces, and meat.. everything. I had never had the patience to actually go to a shake shack but since they had the wait staff I figured why not. and BOY oh BOYYYY am I glad I did! DEF A MUST!

The thing that I never liked about Shea was the lack of food I'd actually want to eat in my regular, non-baseball-game-attending life.  In that vein: WOO HOO! Shake Shack at CitiField is awesome.  The wait is short and worth it, the Shack-cago dog is fabulous and your food is ready practically the minute the order comes out of your mouth.  Goodbye mystery meat hot dogs, hello (and thank you) Danny Meyer!

"Reminds me of Elementary School" For all of you who have NEVER had In and Out or Five Guys... ...I'm sorry. Rarely am I so regretfully compelled to write a review. So I came to NY for the very first time and heard so many great things about Shake Shack...in addition, hundreds of glowing reviews on Yelp for several locations can't be wrong. Or so I assumed. Disappointment. If you've never had In and Out and Five Guys...this place must be good. Traversing NY City, it's hard to find comparable competition to Shake Shack in the (late night) "fast food" category. $10 for one cheeseburger, crinkle cut fries and a tiny soda. The quality is not there to justify it....even in NY. Shakes aside, the tiny, bland burgers and crinkle cut fries remind me of elementary school and the side container of cheese representing an upgrade to "cheese fries" is a joke. Animal style fries nor Cajun fries involve a pricey, yet tiny side container. TOURISTS (hailing from anywhere with an In and Out and/or Five Guys)...AVOID this place at all cost. Try the pizza, bagels and delis, etc that are the true gems of NY. Similarly if everywhere else had a Lombardi's/Grimaldi's quality pizza, people could properly recalibrate what they think is "good pizza".

First thing's first: If you're looking to try this place out, go before the game even starts as the line can be fairly long and you may find yourself standing on line for a couple innings. So by this day and age, everyone knows what Shake Shack is all about. Is it all hyped up as it is supposed to be? Of course, all in relation to the original Shake Shack in Madison Square Park. To the virgin who's never experienced Shake Shack, it's a pretty darn good burger, tender, moist, full of flavor and yummy shack sauce. The fries are crisp and moist on the inside, though the melted nacho-like Velvetta-imitation cheese on top is a bit lacking and unimpressive. I'd probably recommend just getting the fries without the cheese, and save yourself the $1.50 or so on what I consider 2-3 tablespoons of cheese. For some, this might be their best burger and fry experience yet, but to the true Shake Shack aficionado, it is overpriced and slightly subpar to its original counterpart (aka The Shake Shack at Madison Square Park). I haven't been to the original location for quite a while, so I will argue that The Shake Shack has chosen to expand as rapidly as possible (Upper West Side, Upper East Side, Theater District, CitiField and now Miami and Sarasota Springs?). Of course with rapid expansion, comes a standardized almost assembly line way of making their shack burgers at the cost of quality and what I would consider what was one  rather exceptionally made burger. Maybe I'm being too much of a critic, maybe I'm just jealous of their success, but I thought and still do think Shake Shack @ CitiField makes one delicious burger. But something just didn't seem to be right. It seemed to lost some of its glamour. Shake Shack, please don't become another McDonald's, Burger King, or most recently Five Guys. I love Shake Shack and still stand by my word that is probably one of the best burgers in the city (not considering $20+ Kobe beef burgers, etc.).

This review is for Shake Shack in "Times Square" (Really it's just 8th Avenue) My biggest shock surprise was the short line when we got there.  I ordered my usual 'Shroom burger and beer and was please as usual and happy as a clam.  By the time we walked out, the line was half way down the block.  Guess we came at the right time. Great place for a burger and a beer after a movie/show!  Cheap and good eats. Enjoy!

My co-worker who never leaves Westchester County ventured to Queens to watch the Mets and to try this famous burger he's heard so much about. It was a Wednesday night game against Oakland, so the wait wasn't too long. Unfortunately, I saw why when I got to the front of the line - they had precooked the burgers and I was handed a lukewarm one as soon as I placed my order. He said it wasn't too bad and I told him that he didn't know what he was missing, by not trying it FRESH. Ah well, it's still better than anything else at the stadium.

Burger was fine. Fries were cold and rubbery. Shake was frozen solid. Must have been left in freezer. Will never order from my seat again because I don't believe they would have had the audacity to serve me in that fashion had I been at their storefront in the right field area.

I went with my boyfriend to see the Mets v. Cubs and he is the Cubs fan while I barely care about baseball in general so long story short, I volunteered to wait in this obscene line.  It really is crowded.  Sheesh.  Their options are limited but effective.  I got us Shack Burgers, one order of regular fries, one order of cheese fries (way too much cheese!) and a large soda.  That came to something around $33 I believe.  The cashier was confused when I handed him cash.  Apparently they don't see much of that (his words). Shake Shack is expensive in general so while it is marked up a bit for being in the stadium, I didn't feel ripped off when comparing this location to Madison Square Park.  I don't know why someone would get a hotdog from here but they also seemed popular. If you have never had Shake Shack and this is your one opportunity, just do it.  Then you can say you have had it.  But if you live near another location in the city, then don't waste the time it takes to stand on the line and just get food elsewhere.

Maybe it's the location but this was the worst Shake Shack burger I've had. Not that I am a huge fan of their burgers to begin with but quite honestly, a Big Mac would have probably tasted better than the one I had last night at the stadium. It was lacking the 'burger grill' flavor and the patty was thin. Cheese fries were an even more of disappointment. Soggy to the core.  What I don't understand is how is it possible that the line is still the longest of all concession stands.

I did wait on that line again since I was with someone who had never been there. It was my 3rd time and the special order was a LOT faster this time. My companion enjoyed the fries a LOT..said they were probably better than Nathans fries which is huge. Anyway..next season I'll go back again. :)

Decided to jump on the long line at Citi Field yesterday. I thought the line would move slowly but it went at a brisk pace. Anyway.. I had a special order (no cheese/sauce) so I had to wait a little longer but it was worth the wait. The burger was great! The fries were average. Along with the drink it was $14 which isn't bad considering Ball Park food prices. I'd wait on that line again. :)

This is a limited menu of the original Shake Shack but delicious! I would suggest going early and getting your meals right away. The lines are long during game play and the eating area is limited. The Shack-Cago Dog blows the Nathan's Dog out of the ballpark.  Shake Shack is a homerun!

I love Shroom Burger and French fries here. The burger was cooked perfectly, it melted into my mouth, the fries were crunchy and not too salty. However, you have to be a bit patient, because the lines are always long.
Hey Jake..  thanks for replying to my shake shack horrendous post. Is there a way I can give you my email etc privately? Thanks

Hi Rod, Thanks so much for your feedback. I'm so sorry about your experience at Shake Shack. It sounds like we really dropped the ball this time, as you certainly shouldn't have to wait that long to order your food. We can do better than what you experienced, so we'd love to invite you back to the Shack if you're willing. What's your email address, so we can grab your details? Thank you again, Jake

Service is HORRENDOUS!  Whoever is in charge of staffing should be fired. I know it's huge customer base at a ballgame but with proper staffing shouldn't be more than 45 mins EVER.  90 MINUTES and missed 4 innings of game. 1 cashier, waaay too few staff to handle customers.

I'm not sure what's worse. The fact that a simple burger, fries and a large soda cost $17 (THAT'S SEVENTEEN DOLLARS. SEVEN-TEEN. ONE-SEVEN. TWENTY MINUS THREE. TEN PLUS SEVEN. 17.), or the fact that I not only willingly and knowingly paid it, but did so at a game where the Mets lost to the Diamondbacks 14-1!!! Wow. I mean wow. I really thought that the Shake Shacks in the city were expensive at $11-12 for the same order. It shocks and disturbs me that they get away with this. Now, I know that people have somewhat of a choice (aka don't buy it...), but STILL!!! If it weren't were the fact that I had free tickets to that lousy game, I most certainly would have kept walking past this place. Being Shake Shack, the food was definitely tasty, though nowhere damn near it's price tag. Amusement parks and sports arenas are known for their outrageously priced concessions. I get this. However, the home team should at least be WORTH it if their stadium's pricing is going to steal my wallet's innocence... With a 14-1 loss, I went home broke and disappointed. Ugh. Next time I'm at a Mets' game, I will be sure to eat beforehand. No way will I ever pay that much for fast food again!

I dont know what they do to cook that burger to be so juicy and delicious, but it's better than the other Shake Shacks I've had in the city. The first location in Queens and the second it's in Terminal 4 at JFK Airport.  Many compare the Shack burger to In-N-Out burger and I have to say that Shake Shack is wayyyy better than In-N-Out. It was worth the wait, only waited the first inning, good thing for the large screen to catch the first pitch and the game.

Saw the Mets play against the Angels (A loss, unfortunately) and braved the long lines for some Shake Shack. I normally don't have the patience to wait for it and just get a hotdog instead, but the game was basically over in the first inning anyway. Let me tell you, Shake Shack is worth the wait. The shakes are addictive and delicious. We got a 'Shroom burger and a SmokeShack burger. Something about the shack sauce really makes these burgers perfect. The SmokeShack comes with a substantial amount of bacon and a nice handful of cherry peppers that add the right amount of kick.

The line here at Citi Field's Shake Shack  is ridiculous. I think it took us 3 full innings to finally get to the front of the line to take our order. The food is good, but it is overpriced compared to the ones in Manhattan. Ordered the Single Shake, Cheese Fries and the Black/White frozen custard. The burger was smaller than expected, but the meat patty was delicious. It was a tad over seasoned, but still yummy. The cheese fries were drizzled with a liquidfied cheese and the frozen custard was drinkable with a single straw - meaning its not very thick (which is a good thing). I like Shake Shack since its comparable to In-n-Out on the west coast. If it came to the west coast, I would be torn and wouldnt know which one would be better, so its best that these two are on the opposite sides of the country. My advice, if you are touring NYC, dont get Shake Shack at here, go to the other locations in Manhattan. on a side note, I came on 6.8.10 - Mets v Padres and I have to say (for this game - GO METS). It was 1-0. Mets =)

The line is out of control... that said, I stand on it every time I come to Citi Field. The burgers are very tasty, but I have been told not as good as the location in Manhattan. The real reason I wait on line is the Milkshake. Even if I eat somewhere else in the park, I find myself on line that huge snaking line just for a thick, rich shake. What makes them stand out is the custard base, delicious. A great way to wash down the bad taste the Mets leave in your mouth.
