Shack-ago dog, fries and shake hit the spot. Was it better than a Chicago dog...no, but I was in NY and it wasn't bad. Fries and shake were filling. Price, steep for the three at $18, but eh, its NY. Line was 25 minutes. Last game of the season and it was fun to be there and try this place I heard about.

I finally braved the line at Shake Shack at Citi Field, having avoided it every other time I've been there. I figured Shake Shack was the best bet, since I had to eat anyway, and I had money to burn. There are TWO lines to stand on, both going to different sides of the Shack -- right and left. Choose wisely! The line I went on moved rather quickly, all things considered. I definitely had my food within a half hour, and was able to watch the game on the screen behind me. I got on line before the game began, and had my food by the second inning or so. I ordered my usual -- the Shack burger -- but went a little different fries-wise and got the Frisky Fries, which I don't think I've seen at any other location. These fries are cheese fries with a spicy tomato sauce AKA a big ol' mess in a cardboard box. The fries proved to be way too sloppy and icky, and not all that flavorful, so I would certainly NOT get those again. However, the burger tasted about the same as other shack burgers I've gotten in NYC, so that was a plus. I also got the Goose Island Honkers Ale, which was their "premium" beer on tap. I do believe you get slightly more beer here for the buck, but it could just be an illusion. I returned to the Shack after the 8th inning to brave the line once again, this time for a shake (I had digested the burger, fries, and beer since the 3rd inning or so). I ordered the black and white shake, and I assume that they must shut down the shake machines at a certain time, because in less than a minute, the guy put the shake in front of me, all smiles. Clearly, it was a pre-made shake. Wasn't too happy about that, because it still cost me $6.25, and it had probably melted a bit at that point. The worst part is, it tasted like a straight-up chocolate shake. It was really thick, and was no where near the black and white shake I had gotten at the Times Square location. Hey, bozo, I asked for a black and white! The least they can do is clearly state that by a certain time, the shakes are pre-made and served that way, in order to allow the machines to be cleaned and shut down by the game's end. Shake Shack is a solid choice at Citi Field, but only if you have the patience, time, and moolah to acquire a meal here. Otherwise, there are numerous eateries surrounding you that all want your dollar.
A good ball game burger. I highly recommend arriving early because the line for Shake Shack during the game is very long.

I have waited on the line in Madison Square Park for a delicious order of shake shack, but sitting on a comparable line for something that just says shake shack was less than worth it. It may have the name but it does not have the product as I was deeply disappointed in this facade. The burgers were way over cooked and tasted like fast food with the amount of salt and pepper drenched on my burger. My black and white shake tasted like it had been pre made and been sitting in a container for about a month. I need to go back to the city to remember what a real shake shack burger and shake tastes like.

Came to see the Mets do their thing with a group of work friends and we all voted on getting Shake Shack. The line wasn't too bad--I'd say we waited about 10 to 12 minutes to order, and then our food came out pretty fast. To those complaining about the line: I'm sure you've waited longer for Shake Shack in Madison Sq Park, because I know I have. My burger tasted just like any other Shake Shack burger, but I think these are pre-made and left out to sit. Also the prices were higher than normal, but you always end up paying more at a stadium. Pro-tip: get two beers when you order so you don't have to head back down during the game, at least that's what I did!

The shake shack lines at citi field... Always long The food... Always amazing I often hear people ask "is it worth waiting on this line" and my response is an automatic and emphatic "yes!" Citi Field has better food options than most ballparks and sure you can skip the line and get stuff elsewhere, but this is an absolute must if you're headed to the ballpark (especially those doing ballpark tours, etc.) Leave yourself extra time as you may miss the first pitch if you head in too close to game time. Grab a double burger with fries, find your seats and make sure to shout LET'S GO METS between bites of the deliciousness that is Shake Shack
Burgers are just as good as a regular location. Line is always long but does seem to move. I don't feel like standing in line for 30+ mins. Baseball & burgers how can you go wrong!!

So was it worth the 20 min wait in line?  Only if the Mets are losing 14 to 1 in the 8th inning and you have nothing better to do, as in my situation. The Shack burger was okay, not the best I've had but being from Texas, I am quite picky with my beef.  The bread is amazing!  The texture pairs well with the well seasoned lean beef.  The patty is thin enough to absorb the seasonings and the edges are crispy for the added crunch on the first  bite. We got 2 shakes, the black and white shake (basically chocolate) and Vanilla shake.  These are very custardy and sweet, not the best shakes to go with burgers but amazing by themselves or with frites. The price is outrageous, as stated by some of the other reviewers, but with a 20 min line, who's gonna change their mind? Overall, not bad, but don't know what the rave is all about.

Really?  This is what all the fuss is about.  Maybe this one isn't that good cause it's at Shea, I mean citi field, but really. Burgers are ok, probably better than the other food stands for sure. The hot dog thing was okay (chicago style dog) The shakes were good. The fries though were GREAT! Everything is totally over prices of course.
Everyone loves Shake Shack, who doesn't? You will have to wait for at least 20-30 minutes once the game starts, so my recommendation will be get in line before 6 or 6:30 to avoid the crazy line!

For a fast food burger - the gold standard.  Incredibly juicy and flavorful, very fresh, wonderful brioche bun.  Expensive, yes, but everything is at CitiField.  Their vanilla shake is to die for, as is the frozen custard (SOOO much better than Carvels').  Fries are ok - but I actually prefer Nathan's.  Lines are ridiculous - as others have said, get there way early before the game, or accept it that you'll miss a couple innings (watch them on the projection screen behind the scoreboard while you're waiting). Skip the Shackago Dog - this is NYC, we don't need all that crap on a frank, certainly not celery salt (what the...!!!).  Go directly to the burger and a shake, and you'll be a very, very happy camper! Now, they really REALLY need to open a second location at the ballpark, as they wisely did with Blue Smoke - what on earth is wrong with the facility and restaurant management, can't they SEE that?  Lines are insane, which is the only reason we don't eat here more often when we come to Mets games.  A second location at the Promenade food court, please, guys, come ON!!!

Shake Shake rules in the burger and dog category.  The Chicago dog was sooo tasty! Never had one before, can't wait to have another, so tasty, crunchy and spicy in all the right ways, love it!  The fries with cheese and spiced onions were magical , couldn't figure out why they serve these with one of those little pitchforks, they should have given me a little shovel because that's what I wanted to do with those fries...shovel them in!!!!!
Scored the chocolate cookies n cream special shake here, which was a surprise because they reportedly accept no vouchers, no GCs, and participate in no promos.
did you know if youre in the lower seats, the waiters will get you a shack burger for only 6 bucks!! THE BURGERS ARE ACTUALLY  cheaper in the lower sections 100-200

this place sucks, the line takes forever and took 3 innings of waiting and when you finally get on line it takes like 2 seconds to get the food.  the prices are ripoff for such a small ass burger.  the burger is the size of mcdonalds cheeseburgers, but they are really really good. the shakes are okay, nothing spectacular. the fries are actually really good, my favoritepart. and dont get the shack dog or shacago dog, whatever hot dog thats called cuz they put so much crap on it that it all falls off when you bite it. if you are getting it in the city i would recommend it, but not at citifield, get food at the regular stands and enjoy the game. :)

My boyfriend and I thought we would stick it out on the horrendous line but it actually moved pretty fast.  The burgers were great, and the black & white shake was delicious. I would recommend getting there really early, before the game even starts.

Damn fine little burger.  Apparently, from a local, I just had to have one of these because they're the bom-dot-com-bomb-diggity.  Super small, and a little greasy quite frankly.  But the special "shake" sauce and potato bun make it worthwhile.  I didn't think my black and white/can't we all just get along/unity milkshake was all that. This park has nothing on my San Francisco Giants AT&T Park food fare, though.  Not even close, nosirreebob.  That said, walking away for only $12.50 at Citi Field puts Willie's field to shame.

I love Shake Shack because they have the best burger and fries I have ever eaten in my life. All the burgers and fries are made fresh and are not processed. Their handspun milkshakes are also the best. This really adds to the CitiField experience of watching a Mets game. The major drawback is waiting at least an hour, about 1 or 2 innings to finally get your food. Hopefully, they can implement a system to make the lines go quicker. I also wish they had more locations in Queens.

I like to have a burger from Shake Shack every once in a while, and if the Mets happen to be playing a home game when I get a craving, then I'll head here to Citi Field and try to get some cheap promenade tickets last minute so I can enter the stadium to get in line for some Shake Shack!! Sometimes this is more convenient than going to Manhattan or Long Island for another Shake Shack location, or cheaper than going to the other Queens Shake Shack (since that one is in JFK and you'd have to buy a plane ticket). They've got TVs everywhere so you can watch the Mets play an inning or two (or three) while you wait in line to order your burger. It's a bit pricier here, and occasionally the burger patty has been greasier than normal, but the staff is trying to get you your burger fast so you can go watch the baseball game you paid to see, right?

Worth the wait, especially if you have an iPhone handy to distract you.  They have a big TV screen in the area and a live audio feed of the game, which should be enough for all but the most die hard fans as long as it's not a big spot. There are two lines--it seemed like maybe the rightmost one was a little shorter and maybe even moved a little faster when I was there. The food is the same quality as the Madison Square Park Shake Shack, though the presentation is a lot more rushed and there's a decent chance it sat under a heat lamp for a minute or two.  The cheeseburgers are amazing, and for me the real draw.  The fries are run-of-the-mill.  The black and white milkshake I had was good, but between that and two cheeseburgers it was all so filling I couldn't finish. The Mets version also sells Pepsi fountain sodas.

Was in town recently, and I decided to go to a Mets game with some friends. We waited over 45 minutes in line for Shake Shack, after hearing that this was the In N Out of the East Coast. The line moved briskly, and sure enough I finally got my double shack with fries and a chocolate shake. The fries were very salty and served Nathan's style, but nonetheless tasty. They were good, but I would not order them again. As for the main event, the burger, it was dry, overcooked, and the cheese did not blend well with the meat at all. I've had better at my local Burger King. It was bland, at best, as the meat was so dry and overcooked. It just tasted like it was missing something. And finally, the shake, very rich and distinct flavor. It wasn't bad, but it was not great either. It was way too sweet and rich (chocolate) to be considered great. I'd get the Chocolate-Vanilla mix if I returned here again, probably not as strong in flavor. Overall, it was not at all worth the 45 minute wait. Lots of hype, to no avail. Dry, overcooked burgers, salty fries, and very rich shakes. You'll find me at Blue Smoke next time. -Joe

This was such an authentic-feeling experience. The food was completely new to me (I hadn't had much exposure to Jewish food prior to this) and it was really cool to try something different and rooted in tradition. The decor is so fascinating and perfectly on theme, which adds a lot to the experience. Service was good. Overall it just felt like such a special, classic NYC spot. I'm really glad I came here; it was very cool experience all around!

Did you know that Russ and Daughters was the FIRST business to add "& Daughters" to their name, and at the time it was considered to be highlu controversial? Lox: 10/5 Bialy/onion/tomato/cream cheese: 3/5- not enough schmear, tomato looked beautiful but was mealy, my server refused my request for the bialy to be cut in half (having dental work) Service: 1/5: server was honestly, awful. Extremely preoccupied chatting with his coworker. I requested scallion creamcheese and for my bilay to be cut vertically due to some dental work. He said "not possible" on the cutting but confirmed the scallion cream cheese. I was brought regular cc. After reviewing the menu, not even sure the R+D cafe has more than one cream cheese flavor but surely he could have informed me of that when I ordered? I did try to flag him down, verballu and eventually w a raised hand, he was again, too preoccupied chatting a few feet away to look in my direction. He finally came over when I had ONE BITE left, attempting to pour coffee into my non existent coffee mug and asked "food taste good?" After said last bite was already in my mouth. I am hopeful it was just poor service/ they dont have their "A team" on a slow week day. Regardless, the host was professional and greeted me warmly, the food was decent, I would come again if I was in the area. Otherwise I would suggest the other Russ and Daughter's locations. Barney Greengrass (if you know, you know), still takes the cake for me. Ambiance + decor : 5/5- beautiful, accesible, comfortable restaurant, clean and good lighting, can sit and stay a while Entrance and restaraunt are accesible for individuals with mobility barriers

Had an amazing time at the restaurant despite the 20 minute wait! Our waiter was so nice and helpful, and even slipped us a few extra bagels, yum! My friend and I were extremely hungry, so we decided to go for the 4 person platter between the two of us, and it was a great decision! The various smoked salmon was so delicious and went down smooth with the variety of cream cheeses and bagels. The place gets very busy around brunch hours on weekends, but you can pit your name down and go grab a coffee!
Very solid brunch place- we all got the lox bagel plate with greens and a pickle. The vibe is amazing and so is the service. They have amazing quality fish and amazing bagels.

An iconic deli counter and restaurant, this was worth seeking out in NY. It gets busy and they don't do reservations but it moved fast. We got a seat at the counter and service was excellent. The food was outstanding - we tried the smoked salmon, chopped liver, and knishes. Everything was that throwback old school vibe and I loved it. Will return when I'm back in NYC!

Over the river from Jersey City and through the concrete jungle of New York, I walked 3 miles to get to Russ & Daughters. I know what you're asking yourself, and yes, it was worth it. We were fully expecting a wait upon arrival because it was prime time for brunch at 12 sharp. I gotta say I was impressed they were able to accommodate us at all (especially in NYC) because we were rolling 8 deep. After about an hour we were seated. We passed the time at a conveniently located bar next door called Lucky Jack's. Once we were seated we were ready to nosh hard. Our table was right across from where all the meats are prepared and cut, so it was fun to watch as we waited. We ordered two plates of potato latkes and pickles from the barrel from the appropriately titled Noshes section of the menu. The latkes were beautifully golden brown and crisped to perfection. The pickles added a nice acidity to cut the grease from the latkes. I also enjoyed a dill bloody mary, which was much better than the bloody mary I had next door. For my entree I ordered the Bagel and Lox as my best friend who's Jewish has taught me this is the elite combination. I chose the Pastrami-Cured Salmon for my lox option. They lay all the components out on a board, so you can dictate the amount of toppings on your bagel which I enjoyed. The cream cheese was plentiful and tomatoes, red onion, and dill were all very fresh. It all came together and sang on a bagel with a beautifully soft crumb. My cousin also taught me about egg creams during this visit. Based on the name, it isn't something that sounds very appealing to me but boy was I wrong. Come to find out it contains neither eggs nor cream. It's basically like a healthier milkshake, and I am a newfound fan! Thank you, Russ and Daughter for the classic Jewish comfort food experience!

If you like pickled or smoked fish, you'll be in heaven here. In fact, everything on the menu is wonderful. But it's really popular these days, so you'll probably have to wait for a bit before you can get in. Even still, once you're inside, everyone is so friendly. I've done the pickled herring selection before and the salmon board. One of the things that I love about this place is the quality of the bagels and bialys that they give you. Definitely come with a few friends, so you can share the big platters.

I've heard of Russ & Daughters for a while, but never had the chance to make it out. When I finally got the opportunity, I was all in. This is located in LES, and they don't take reservations. However, I arrived around 1:30pm and there was no wait at all! As a party of two, we were prompty seated. I wanted a try a little bit of everything so I decided to go with the Lower Sunny Side, which included eggs, lox and latkes. While the meal was solid, for the price, I can't say I was blown away. There was nothing wrong per say, it just wasn't memorable to me. However, I do know they are famous for their bagels, and this is someting I didn't have a chance to try, so I would like to give it another shot!

A NYC staple, I was looking forward to eating at this restaurant. The service was fine friendly enough, probably something to get accustomed to in NYC. The food was a little pricey but fresh. I like the liver and the smoked fish. The Latkes and the bagels were ok and maybe just an off day for them. Overall, I'd go just to say I've tried it and I'd recommend the place to tourists as well.

I was intending to go to Russ and Daughter's shop, but ended up at their cafe instead.  Which was fine.  They don't offer bagels or bialys to go -- this is a strictly sit-down diner.  They said the wait would be 40min and then seated me 3 min later lol. The decor is retro and kitschy in a good way.  I sat at the bar and the staff were joyful and welcoming.  Reverence and appreciation for the New York Jewish deli heritage pervaded.  That was nice to see, as many of the old deli institutions are now gone. My entire purpose in visiting was to have a Russ and Daughters bialy, as they are one of the few bakeries that still makes a good bialy.  Interestingly, it was only just ok in the cafe, toasted with butter.  It is much better when I make it at home, as the bialy taste comes alive with darker toasting.  Recommend to toast it more for better flavor. I had the bialy with smoked fish chowder, which was excellent but super rich, and a hot coffee.

Russ and daughters are the gold standard for bagels and lox. I have had it shipped across country and loved it. Having it in the city was a wonderful treat The staff was helpful and there really isn't anything like a perfect bagel and lox to start the day!

When you walk into this place, you feel the history they are trying to capture. It has a diner feel with quality, service, and ambiance of finer dining. Ultimate Jewish deli comfort food served with high quality picked and smoked seafood ingredients. Nice because the OG Russ and daughters is take out only. Sometimes you just want to bagel and chill and not be stuck in your apartment. The latkes are life changing. The bagel and shmear tastes exactly like so many bagel shops in NYC try to capture and emulate, with little success. It's always a long wait but if they say 45 minutes, it'll probably be closer to a 20-30 min wait unless you have a huge party of more than 4.

the food is excellent. I ordered the bialy sandwich with pastrami-smoked salmon. they come deconstructed. the fresh dill really kicked this up a notch. I also had the latkes which were delicious. the service was very quick and friendly. knocking off a star because the bar seating is VERY tight. as a plus size gal I wasn't comfy at all and just barely fit. I figured a reservation wouldn't be that important for one person at 11am on a Monday but boy was I wrong. there were many people waiting for their tables and I had to wait a few mins for a bar seat. even when I left around 11:45 this was still the case. I'd recommend a reservation if you can.
Best bagel and lox I've had! We went at around 3pm on a Monday and got super fast and great service. Both our sandwiches were delicious!
Don't know WTF the hype is all about! Absolutely nothing special! Prices require a second mortgage!

I've been wanting to try Russ & Daughters Cafe for a while now so when my friend suggested it, I was really pumped. We ordered the smoked white fish with toasted bialy and smoked salmon with pumpernickel bread.  My friend enjoyed the white fish very much and I enjoyed my smoked salmon immensely. Service was terrific, extraordinarily on point and kind without being intrusive and the place was immaculate. If I had one wish it would be that the portions were a bit bigger as I found myself getting hungry very shortly after we ate.  All in all, it was a wonderful dining experience.

Came here for brunch. Seated within 10 minutes. Service was professional and pleasant. We ordered 1) fresh squeezed orange juice ($7) 2)Deviled Eggs with smoked trout 3) Lower Sunnyside-smoked salmon, sunny side up eggs, and potato latkes 4) Babka French Toast(chocolate and sour cream) Fresh squeeze Orange juice was so refreshing in the morning. Deviled eggs with smoked trout may be my favorite deviled eggs that I have ever tried. Highly recommend! Might try to make it at home. Ordered lower sunnyside to get a sampler of everything popular here. Smoked salmon was solid, potato latkes were good, basically fat hashbrowns. Babke french toast(chocolate and sour cream) tasted sweet and tangy. Solid. Overall, I think I could see this place as our go-to restaurant. Very solid food here and would definitely come back as a regular.

Bagel & Lox ($24) - I found my new favorite bagel. Their pastrami-cured salmon was the best smoked salmon I've ever had because of its freshness and flavor. Their everything bagel was perfectly seasoned as it wasn't too overpowering. Even the cream cheese and tomato were high quality. It's worth trying!

Came in for breakfast, super packed ! Wait was about a hour , welllll worth it !!! Has like an old school diner feel at first , bar seating and small tables on the side .Pretty good variety of options to choose from, but looks like most based around fresh salmon and caviar that they have displayed in a case . We order the lox plate , and a omelette, I think had mushrooms and spinach and some really good feta !!! Definitely a must try spot !!

Simply amazing the atmosphere the food quality and service. I got an chocolate egg cream. The chopped liver sub glutenfree everything bagel and lox GF everything bagel chive cream cheese and acutremonts. Its Simply thr best GF bagel I've ever had i asked the waitstaff mutiiple times to verify. This is a must when in NYC  an institution that  my family alwase told me about.

A NY Staple that you should experience. At least that is what they say.  If I was rating just the bagel, it would be maybe 2-3 stars. However, I am rating the experience.  From the decor when you walk into the service attire, I felt special being there.  The coffee was hot and good.  We opted for a platter with smoked whitefish and smoked nova.  It came with the tomato and capers and onions.  Presentation was a 10 star for me.  It looked delightful.  The bagels just fell a little flat to me. Nothing stood out.  The ET seasoning was scattered and not consuming the outside of the bagel. I also felt a little rushed, but I do understand that they have a lot of people wanting to experience this like I did. Do I need to go back-no. Am I glad that I went-absolutley!

I love it here! I was told it would be a 30 minute wait and it ended up being a 6 minute wait so don't venture too far and don't hesitate to put your name on the list then bop around the neighborhood. From the hotel I was staying in, I walked past the R&D deli location en route to the cafe. The deli is your best bet for grab and go and a solid option for bagel sams eaten on the sidewalk. Besties, if you're looking for a more robust sit-down experience, ya gotta come here instead. I love the special touches and the iconic New York experience-ness of it all. The drawings on the walls, the menu setup, all of it! None of that compares to the thinly slices, perfectly smoked lox. I also enjoyed the matzoh ball soup, chowder (sooo good), and a mimosa. This spot has booze! The classic board is a MUST and something I would order again and again. Skip the cold and somewhat dense deviled eggs, otherwise have fun! Our server was fabulous and food comes out at a quick clip. If you're lucky, you'll get seated next to the magic (kitchen) and watch it all happen.

Cruised down to the LES to get some Jewish deliciousness and R&D did not fail. It is super clean, no mental visual of large rats running around the kitchen (IYKYK) and the food did not disappoint. I would order a little differently--would not have the horseradish cream cheese on the lox bagel--it added nothing, the soup was perfection, and I think next time I'll get the creme fraiche caviar topping on the latkes. Services was spectacular, but I have to admit that the server calling us "my friend" 50 times grew tiresome. But oy! There's no complaints here. As MOT's we left happy. And that, my friends, is no small feat.
Friendly server. Classic bagel really hit the spot. Traditional diner look with things done simply but well.

The highly raved place for brunch, so I finally decided to go with couple friends. We ordered a variety of dishes to share. An unanimous favorite was the smoked herring appetizer, it wasn't overly salty or slimy. The smoke salmon was delicious, but it' wasn't a particularly exceptional smoke salmon that we haven't had anywhere else. Felt it was a bit overpriced for smoke salmon with cream cheese.

Overall (A+) This place is really good and provide excellent service. Food (A+) Got the bagel and lox's and bagel and cream cheese. Both were excellent. The food quality is excellent. Value (A-) You pay a slight premium for the brand but it is not too bad Service (A+) Excellent caring customer service. Can't beat it. Try it out if you are in the neighborhood try it out.i will get from here everytime I am in town

Amazing breakfast spot - stopped here before our tour at the Tenement Museum. Delicious, and super fresh foods - would definitely recommend everything that we got: the cinnamon babka French toast, the  farm egg omelet, the potato latkes, the bagel & bread basket, and the coffee!! Service was as great as the food - but you might have a wait during peak times and this is a hot spot in the neighborhood.

I know there's a ton of hype around this place, and everyone has an argument for the best bagel in NY, and the truth is NYC is full of amazing bagels. But I'm glad I trekked to Russ & Daughters because the hype was real. The Tuna Salad here is to die for. TO DIE FOR. I've always liked tuna salad, but I've never had one that I would trek for, travel for, take 5 different trains for. I would for this. This tuna, plus their signature scallion cream cheese equals heaven. In my saddest moments, I think about this bagel to lift my spirits.

My husband was raving about this place having the best Bloody Marys he's ever had in the whole country! So of course we had to try this during our visit to new york. It didn't make reservations so it was about 30 minute wait before we were able to be seated, considering it was a Saturday morning I think I was pretty reasonable. We ordered a number of dishes to Sharon including the double eggs, soft scramble caviar and matzo ball soup. Each order the classic bagel and lots which was amazing.. we also got the ride putting for dessert. The Bloody Marys blew my mind, they were even better than my husband described! This place was amazing and exceeded my expectations. Highly recommend!

This was one of my favorite brunch spots in New York. You can't skip out on the latkes and finishing with a sweet French toast was the perfect combination. The applesauce and sour cream really put it together. Their Scottish smoked locks was really good, but have to come back and try the pastrami smoked lox. The blueberry soda was refreshing! The service was really good, our waiter gave us some notes and recommendations of other places. Their boo seating is large and comfortable.

This has been one of my favorite restaurants on earth and it's my first stop in NYC. That said, removing my beloved belly lox from the menu is a sin and crime against appetizing. Omg! Omg! Omg! Omg! Omg! Omg!

Russ and Daughters feels a bit like a time capsule when you walk in. The staff is friendly and efficient. Everything we ordered was delicious. The smoked salmon is top notch. If I were to go back I would order The Classic again. It was the perfect balance of smokey, fresh, and briney. So yummy! The orange juice is fresh squeezed and the coffee was good.

PLEASE don't get discouraged by the wait time.  Waited an hour,  but took this opportunity to walk around and explore! Food was absolutely perfect.  We ordered a little bit of everything.  Appetizer,  bagel board, mushroom omelet,  and French toast- cinnamon with two cocktails- Miriam s cup and break-fast martini.  FABULOUS! SERVICE WAS GREAT AND QUICK! Ambiance- great music,  great food,  ambiance was just right. Definitely will be returning next year!

I've never been a fan of bagels, but I changed my mind after eating here. My friend recommended Russ & Daughters for their lox and bagels, and I was pleasantly surprised by how high quality they were! The fluffy cream cheese was rich yet light, and paired well with the various toppings that came with it. I also ordered the potato latkes, bursting with flavor and texture! Our waiter was very personable and attentive, checking if we needed water refills frequently. The cafe itself is cozy yet elegantly decorated- I enjoyed peering through the glass to explore the various bagels and fillings they offered!
We had such a great time. TJ was our server and he was PHENOMENAL. He had the best vibe and all of his recommendations hit the spot! So happy we went there:)))

This place is amazing, I've been to their store on Houston but first time in the cafe. Exceptional food and impeccable service. The best part was when one of the owner ( also one of the daughters as in Russ & Daughters) came by to see how our lunch was. It was the highlight of our meal.

After visiting Russ & Daughters, we met a friend at the Russ & Daughters Café. It was worth it, but be prepared for a bit of a wait. The café isn't large, but it's light, bright, and tidy. I ordered The Classic: Gaspe Nova smoked salmon with cream cheese, red onion, capers, and tomatoes. They also ask for your choice of bagel--I had a plain one toasted. It was delicious and really hit the spot. My husband ordered the Matzo Ball Soup, which was flavorful, with chicken and matzo balls--a comforting dish. He also had the pickled herring filet with pumpernickel, which he enjoyed (though it's not my favorite). My friend had the Potato Latkes with wild salmon roe and crème fraîche, and she was also able to get applesauce and sour cream on the side, for a bit of both. They were delicious. We ordered chocolate egg creams, and my husband had a house-made grape soda. If you're looking for Coke or Pepsi, they don't offer those, but I appreciated the unique house-made drinks. Service was friendly and helpful. It wasn't an inexpensive lunch, but it was worth it for the food and quality time with a dear friend. It was nice to be able to sit down comfortably and enjoy our meal. The café is about a five-minute walk down Orchard Street from the original location. Cheers!

Went in during the lunch rush and got some matzo ball soup which rocked my world. The staff was awesome and attentive. Brought home a bagel with lox for my spouse at home and it was perfection (got the goat cream cheese which was great). FYI at this spot they don't do 'take out' per se so they'll bring you the food to pack up yourself to take home as leftovers. I don't mind that but just a heads up.

While visiting NY we had to go to Russ & Daughters Cafe! We went on a Tuesday mid-day. It was busy but we only had to wait about 10 min and got a booth. The host was very friendly and our server was awesome (sorry, we forgot his name. He's tall, thin build with a mustache). I had the Classic board with an everything bagel and the smoked whitefish chowder was amazing! It was so delicious, I wish I could have packed it up and brought it home! It was a great meal and great visit!

My first upscale Jewish Diner experience and egg creme and shrub drink! Russ & Daugther now has several locations in NYC, and this one is lower east side, very close to the Russ & Daugther store and takeaway. This is sit down, and no reservations taken, we walked in and waited a 20 minutes before we sat down (we got a coffee at a different location to wait). The restaurant is immaculate with a super welcoming bar area and booths with tons of smoked fish, cured fish on the menu. The upscaleness comes from the caviar they sell. At Russ & Daughters with my Jewish friend, I got to try egg creme - which unlike it's name does not have egg or cream, it's a light chocolate milkshake think nesquick with soda water and it's delightful. I'd seen it a lot in the movies from the soda shop days and I've always wanted to try it. I also got a beet shrub: a drink made with a fruit-infused vinegar syrup and sparkling water. I'm a sucker for any beet juice drink. The food was lovely, very good Jewish deli food elevated - the portion sizes are controlled here, not like the old school delis where you meats are the size of your head. I rate this place 5 stars bc I think about that shrub. We did have a small tin of caviar, and it was a delightful experience. Would for sure come back and recommend to people who enjoy an upscale diner experience.

Who knew I needed caviar on my bagel. Well new bar has been set on extravagant eating. Coffee selection is just drip but there's an espresso place really close if you are like me and need that. Service is great as you grab a number on way in and order when called. Highly recommend this place and can't wait to visit again
The host was very rude and unaccommodating to me and my family of 5. We offered to split up to get tables quicker but he totally brushed us aside.

Going to RUSS and Daughter IS like being back to my childhood in Brooklyn. The smells of the smoke fish is elegant and brings back memories of a kinder gentle time with my family on SUNDAY MORNING. It's a cultural experience I wish everyone can experience. Your readers must take the time to have this opportunity they earn the 5 stars. Irwin Z

Every restaurant article points to Russ & Daughters - a must try. They did not disappoint! The latkes were my favorite!! They come with a few different toppings - roe and cream, apple sauce and sour cream.  Both are such good options. The apple sauce and sour cream are actually better than you would think. Nice surprise actually. I also really loved the babka French toast, perfect texture. We sat at the bar/counter. The waiter/bartender was super friendly and helpful. We had a great conversation with him! Really nice experience here and we will definitely come back!

The lox bagel was good but the service was horrible. Ignore the entire time not even ask if I need anything else or offer more coffee. Plus attitude when asked ONE question when ordering. My server was Cory at the bar

When in the city I try to taste all of the best NYC has to offer.  And this is no exception. Service is on point. Latke is the best I have EVER had. Famous for the pickled Herring so I had to try it. It did not disappoint.  Amazing! I will be back to explore more of the menu.
Nice sit down restaurant. Definitely worth the waiting time and being sat at the counter.

This place is one of my neighborhood favorites for brunch. It is quite popular for brunch so it takes some planning, but inside feels spacious when seated. The staff are pleasant and considerate. I liked when my waiter brought over my drink with 2 straws without me asking when he knew that I was going to share with my partner. One of my favorite dishes is probably the Lower Sunny Side. The Halva Ice Cream is good too. I would recommend this place for brunch in the LES.

I'm not lucky enough to live in NYC.  (I make do, here on the Third Coast.)  However, I've now ordered four times from R&D (once for myself, thrice as gifts to loved ones).  We've all been delighted. I'd never heard of them until I listened to a great NPR story* about this "appetizers" outlet and its history.  I was already sold by the name alone ("and daughters"), but hearing how the lox is sliced was the clincher. Well, the service and attention to detail are amazing.  The lox really is "Oh my God" good . . . and, as an unexpected bonus, turns out they have a delicacy that's been impossible to find here:  pickled green tomatoes.  Even their merchandise is top notch (e.g., a lovely and well-made spreader; a nifty, very cool mug). R&D seems to be going great guns, but I've been happy to be able to do my part to support them. _________________________________________ * ( https://www.npr.org/2025/09/06/nx-s1-5382315/russ-daughters-niki-russ-federman-josh-russ-tupper)
This place was so YUM! Very worth the 1 hour wait. I will forever be thinking about the latkes and salmon roe. I am also a salmon Benedict fan, and this one was scrumptious.

Made a quick stop at Russ & Daughters this morning for a light breakfast. The Orchard Street location is really cool, it throws back to an old soda fountain/diner. Cool marble tiles and counter tops and great decor elsewhere, too. The couple staff I interacted with were smiley and kind.  I really enjoyed the whitefish croquettes and the rugelach.  The croquettes were piping hot and nested on a dill sauce. The rugelach were crispy and sweet.  Their menu is pretty expensive, too.
Such a cute spot and I love the retro design, but my bagel was unfortunately hard and the disassembled aspect made it messy and difficult to eat.

Still thinking about this place! Visited NYC and was on a mission for a good bagel with lox and this place did not disappoint. The cafe is a bit on the smaller side but it is warm and bright. This location does not serve the bagel sandwiches seen at other locations and instead has a few bagel board options. We had the Apple French toast as our sweet breakfast treat and it was also delicious. Highly recommend!

Everything was great. I had the matzo ball soup and potato pancakes. I had some of my friend's French toast and it was phenomenal as well. Great authentic place. The cold brew coffee was delicious too!

Can we give it 6 stars?  Only waited two minutes for a table which is unusual. Sam, our waiter, was super. We started with the Deviled Eggs with Smoked Trout which were creamy and delicious. Paired the eggs either a bowl of Smoked Whitefish Chowder that the kitchen split into two bowls for us. The chowder was our fondest memory from a previous visit and it didn't disappoint. Creamy but not too rich, flavorful but not too Smokey. Shared a classic nova board with an extra bagel. And, of course, a side of potato latkes. The nova was very mild and sliced paper thin. Very delicate. Wish there had been another slice or two but.... The latkes were thick, crispy on the outside and creamy inside. Had to try them; enjoyed them; might not do again. Finished with coffee (strong) and cinnamon Rugelach that were flaky and tasty. Everything we remembered and more. A really special brunch for us.

Came by for breakfast the other day and it was a decent experience. Russ & Daughters is in the Lower East side and is featured in the Michelin guide as a Bib Gourmand. The cafe was super clean and modern with elevated pricing. Staff wore a white Russ & Daughters lab coat as their front of the house uniform. Ordered the smoked salmon eggs Benedict and it was decent. The bread was freshly cut and the smoked salmon was fragrant with the taste of preservatives. The actual poached egg was decent although I've had better. Their hollandaise sauce was good and not too heavy. Service by the staff was quick and efficient. $31/head for breakfast after tax and gratuity
As usual, amazing. My server at the bar, Erik, was so helpful. Love the recs. Bagel fresh, pickles great.

A true NYC classic, a must try!! I personally love Russ & Daughters Cafe and have been to it a few times over the years. Service / Ambiance / Vibe: - excellent service from the staff at large, when I went on 12/6 our waitress was very attentive and nice - Cool to dine at the cafe of such a historic NYC business - the decor and view of the kitchen really gives you that NY Diner feel Food: I love the food, the bagel - lox - cream cheese platter is fire. the SOUPS are incredible, menu at large is interesting and full of good food. As other reviewers have noted, it's a pricier option....if you just want a bagel sandwich at the best price - then yes obviously go to your local bodega and just get that. But if you want the full experience AND if I had to guess I'm sure the food quality and sourced ingredients are much better than a bodega....go to the cafe, have a seat and enjoy a great dining experience.

Worth traveling across town for ! I actually found their other location first, which seemed more like a grab-and-go kind of place - it had a line out the door so I decided to pass. Then I found this location and I'm so glad I did ! (They're actually relatively close to each other which is awesome) Seating & wait time I was alone and the wait was about 30ish minutes. However, I got a text from them maybe 10 minutes later that my seat was ready. Luckily I hadn't wandered too far ! They don't have much of a waiting area at the restaurant so I recommend walking around a bit They have stool seating at the bar which is where I sat. Each spot does have hooks under the bar to hang your belongings. They also have table and booth seating further into the restaurant. Staff: They have the most friendly and up beat staff I've ever seen! Everyone was very sweet and welcoming. They also joked around with each other and generally seemed to have a good time working there. Food: I opted for the basic board with salmon. There were so many delicious looking options, but I felt (being alone) that a lot of the options would have been too much for me and better shared. That being said I definitely need to come back with a friend or two to experience more of the menu! Everything on my board was so fresh and flavorful! From the everything bagel to the onions to the salmon. Honestly it blew my mind how such a simple order could be so delicious I also ordered a tea and was given my own small pot. That was great with it being a cold & rainy day. When you sit down you're immediately given a whole bottle of still water which is nice too. Overall this place was amazing and I highly recommend it ! I can't wait to come back!

Another FANTASTIC experience here. From the hostess, to our server, to the manager - everyone here is so nice. The hostess quoted us a 45 min wait when we arrived around 12:30pm for four people, but was able to seat us in half that time. Our waitress, Margot I believe was her name, was extremely understanding when two people in our party were pressed for time due to a show on the other side of time (our fault for getting here late) and made sure our food arrived very promptly. We got amazing suggestions for food from the manager and everything was spot on. We ordered the Ida board for four of us (the smoked salmon is like butter in your mouth!), potato latkes (some of the best I've EVER had), Super Heebster (wow), and the babka French toast for dessert (don't sleep on this one). It was the perfect amount of food for the four of us. I can't say enough good things about Russ and Daughters- one of my favorite spots in the city!

Oh my god the food here was actual heaven. My sister and I came on a weekday around 11am, so off hours a bit, and had a 30 min wait. By the time we were done with our meal over an hour later, the hostess was telling people the wait was over two hours. I've heard the wait on weekends is even worse! All the hype around this place was SO real. My favorites were definitely the Super Heebster and Filet of Pickled Herring. The least exciting dish was probably the Shtetl Board, mostly because it followed two fantastic dishes. There isn't much more to say except that the ambiance is fun and the food is to die for.

No better time than the weekday to walk in and dine at russ and daughters than a weekday at 12pm we started with the potato ladkes - they were juicy, crunchy, and full of flavor. reminded me of an indian pakora. we topped it with creme fraiche and salmon roe which IMO is the way to go. second was the salmon with an every bagel - super delicious and the salmon was insanely juicy and fresh. the everything bagel was a good call because it was doughy but also crunchy since we got it toasted! last and my fav was the challah bread pudding which was more on the pudding / squishy in texture side - super good and sweet if you like pudding. one of my favs from the meal. overall good experience and service was quick. would def recommend and return!

This was my first time at the cafe, which opened up in 2014. The original store has been on Houston St. for over a century. The cafe's breakfast menu has many standouts.  The entrees are original.  You can't find most selections in any restaurant anywhere in the U.S. Check out the menu, which is also available online. Today I had some Gaspe Smoked Salmon and Cream Cheese on a Pumpernickel bagel.   TIP:  mix some fresh dill into the cream cheese for a foodgasmic experience. The rugelach is good, but I have had better elsewhere, like at Armin and Judy's in The Hamptons.  The raspberry at Russ and Daughter's is good, but the cinnamon raisin leaves a lot to be desired.  I wish they had apricot, which is my favorite rugelach flavor, but Russ and Daughters does not make it.  Armin and Judy's does. The service in the cafe was terrific.  I sat at the bar. The decor was sleek and modern. I definitely will be back.

Extraordinary experience with truly unique food. Impeccable drinks selection as well as an adorable atmosphere in the heart of midtown a nook in the wall leading to a beautiful experience of flavorful joy. The only down side would be the wait time on weekends but that just tells you even more how good of a place you are about to get into.

How do I love thee? Let me count the ways... 100% worth the hype. Sent a friend smoked salmon, herring, and caviar cream cheese for her birthday via Goldbelly - she was understandably elated. R&D are on a class  of their own!

Finally get the hype RATING: 9.7/10 (for the lox sandwich) PRO TIP: yes the sandwich is pricey. Yes it is delicious. LOX BAGEL SANDWICH This place has so much hype around it and yes this sandwich is amazing. The high quality ingredients and their thoughtful proportions make for a DELICIOUS breakfast experience, beautifully, richly salty smoked salmon cuts through creamy, delectable cream cheese and capers/red onions add additional tartness and texture. My one area of improvement is that the bagel itself is easily not New York's best bagel, as it is soft but does fight you when you try to take bites off the bagel. However, that almost doesn't matter with how great the interior of the sandwich is. FINAL RANKING: EXCELLENT (terrible / bad / ok / good / great / EXCELLENT)

An iconic name and well-known spot that lived up to its reputation! I've known about Russ & Daughters for YEARS thanks to both Instagram and friends of mine talking about their delicious bagels, fish, and babka. The cafe is separate from the Russ & Daughters Appetizers counter shop which is about two blocks north of the cafe location. We arrived at about 8:15 to meet a friend, the cafe opens at 8:30 but we wanted to make sure we could get a seat; we were not formally "in-line" but happened to be the first to enter when the doors opened and the curtains rose. We were seated in a comfortable booth, though there is counter seating in lieu of a booth if you're ever dining solo. By the time we placed coffee orders the cafe was bustling, and it didn't take long for all booths to fill, so come early if you want a seat! I had iced coffee with oat milk and it was fresh and delicious and very strong. We decided to order a lot and share, which is definitely my recommendation at R&DC. In no particular order, we tried the pastrami Russ, the potato latkes with applesauce, sour cream, roe, and creme fresh, the classic board with a bagel, the plate of sours (pickles and pickled tomatoes), and the chocolate babka french toast. Everything was SO, SO DELICIOUS, and it was great to try bites of everything. That babka... it's out of this world. All the flavors were sharp and fresh and complementary in all dishes. Our server was SO attentive and kind, and there were so many little details that he maintained, including fresh silverware, whisking empty plates away, and checking on us in a warm and non-rushed way throughout the meal. Though the space was packed, it felt cozy and comfortable rather than claustrophobic. This place is so special and feels like an institution - which, with its namesake, it is. I recommend highly! I can't wait to come back and try all sorts of other goodies. PS: if you have time, walk the few blocks to check out the storefront, which is an entirely different (and very unique) experience.

Famous for a reason. Enjoyed a delicious lox bagel and glass of fresh-squeezed orange juice. Admittedly on the pricier side, but enjoyed it nonetheless. The cafe itself is adorable, and the service was excellent.

Went at 1:30 on a Sunday and waiting for 90 minutes. It was nice that we can walk around and then got a text when the table was ready. The place is cute inside and they have nice big booths. Only two restrooms in the back. The food is all mainly breads like challah, bagel, rye and cured and smoked fish. So you got to be in the mood for that when you come. The eggs Benny was $26 and was a bit over priced for what it was. The challah was dry, there was t much flavor in the dish. Needed more hollandaise sauce. I barely tasted it. Eggs were poached well. The smoked salmon was fine, tasted good quality. I got a malted egg cream, it was decent. It's seltzer water with malt flavor and milk. It was good to have something sweet to pair with the salty fish. The waiters were nice but disorganized. They brought out our drink like 5-10 minutes after our food. And were also arguing on the side about our bill for some reason. I unfortunately wouldn't come here again. It's a cute place but long wait, high prices and average food. We split the bill and with each getting a meal and 1 drink it was over $50 a person with tip.

I cannot express the level of disappointment eating at this location of Russ & Daughters.  Maybe it would have been different if I'd traveled to Brooklyn.  Alas, lesson learned. The lox is fantastic - thank goodness.  However, things went way south when they tried to pawn a bagel as a bialy.  I grew up in New Jersey just over the Washington Bridge.  I can tell the difference and they argued with me! Also, what they say is toasted is barely warmed. The day before I ate at Barney Greengrass (which is the real deal), so at least I know where to return to next time.

Cute decor and atmosphere. High expectations, as this is obviously a well known institution. Nothing was absolutely terrible...but nothing was great either. Stingy portion of the pastrami-cured lox. Good quality but not enough to cover the bagel. Pretzel bagel was meh. Way better bagels are out there, all over NYC! Spicy Bloody Mary was decent. Whole experience felt overpriced and touristy.

The grab and go Russ and daughters spot was closed so we decided to come to this cute sit down spot to make sure we got our New York bagel! This place had a 30 minute wait but thankfully we were seated much faster which was nice. This is a spot where you can get a variety of breakfast brunch like food - we ended up ordering: * lox bagel plate - this came with a pumpernickel bagel we chose and came with salmon, cream cheese, tomato, onions and dill. Everything was super fresh and went well together *latkas - these were really yummy - almost kindof like a super crispy hash brown with some onions inside as well and came with salmon roe and creme fraiche. Very flavorful and yummy to say the least Overall, this is a nice solid spot if you are looking for some yummy breakfast food New York style!

My to go spot after my workout. I love the type of food they cater to. They have pickled herring to caviar , boards , noshes platters and etc. trust me you will never get disappointed because their customer service is top notch! Constantly checking and making sure you are well taken cared of . I look forward to this place everytime I finish my workout. And it's just the exact type of food I love to eat! Thank you Russ & Daughters for the excellent service ! I come to try all food in the menu

Let's get one thing straight: there is no other place to do Jewish deli other than here. My husband and I had the $110 platter that consisted of a plethora of bagels Bialy's and breads, butter and cream cheese, tomatoes, capers, onions, smoked white fish, smoked Sable, Salmon, and lox. Such a value and the food is outstanding. The pickles are just so unique -this place belongs and has the status that it deserves. Our waiter, Eric, was a wonderful man offered us extra bagels. Just a great kid. The ambience is unparalleled obviously you're here for that too. Very clean.

Okay where to start with this review... The restaurant...very cute and very Jewish, really liked the vibe Service...good service, nice waiter Food...it was just okay. I've grown up on lox and bagels, so on my scale it was only about a 6/10. The bagel wasn't very doughy, it was toasted but wasn't that flavorful? Even though we got the everything, in my opinion it was a pretty dry bagel. The platter only came with 2 slices of tomato, a few red onion slices and capers w cream cheese. Overall it was okay. I ordered a coffee, a lox and bagel platter, with an extra bagel and cream cheese and that was it. My bill came out to be around $46 with tax and tip. I don't know how it possibly wound up being that much, but I wasn't happy about the price. Mistake? Inflation? I duno..does that amount sound right to you?

I have always wanted to try Russ & Daughters and on this visit I finally did! First of all, the cafe is so cute- classic New York charm without feeling too cramped at all. Our service was excellent- friendly, helpful, professional. I got a vanilla egg cream and my husband tried the house made cream soda. Why don't more places sell egg creams?! Yum! Then I got the smoked whitefish chowder and the "sours" (a bowl of house made pickled). The whitefish chowder was one of the most delicious things I've ever had in my life. Like last-meal on death row good! My husband went more traditional with "the classic" bagel and lox, and a bowl of matzoh ball soup. Everything was amazing! I would have loved to try the babka but I was too full- next time!
Great service! Fresh food. You can't go wrong with bagels and lox. Worth a second and third visit.

The service is great--so friendly and helpful. We love the bagels, shmears, bread, and baked goods. I wasn't overly crazy about the kasha varnishkes--to me it tasted like the barley was old, but it's not a dish that I have ever had before, so maybe that's just what it tastes like. Still, loved the experience.

Came here after hearing and seeing so much hype. For all the chatter and rave reviews, the food was underwhelming to say the least. Ordered a toasted bagel with Lox which came on a wooden platter with onions, capers and salmon. The bagel was NOT toasted as requested and there were a measly two slices of salmon and some tomatoes with cream cheese. They also forgot the egg i had asked for. Also ordered hot coffee which was decent. The ambience was as expected, that of an old school NY diner and it was definitely busy. Service was average as got seating at the counter. The hostess was very kind and polite. I genuinely feel like several bodegas have bagel sandwiches that are SO much better than this place. The menu is overly pretentious and complicated (imho). Paid $30 for the above... could have gotten a MUCH better meal with 1/4th the price at another 'no-frills' place and would have been much happier. Feel like this is a tourist trap and most likely not come back again based on the experience...

Great service with a clean, classic diner/deli vibe. We ordered The Classic Board with a plain bagel, Eggs Benny, and the yogurt, fruit, and granola. A must try if you're a fan of fresh, smoked salmon- my first time trying it and wasn't disappointed. If you're in the area, I highly recommend you try this 100+ year historical NYC staple.

My mom was friends with one the Russ daughters so this business is sorta in my blood.  Our family has been feasting on their supple lox and unctuous sable, babka and hopjes (Dutch coffee candies) for over a century.  Being able to lunch at this casual and comfy restaurant is a wonderful option.  Of course I order the bialy with cream cheese, capers and lox from the friendly server - when she gave us a few hopjes at the end my soul was full. It's a bright place, windows front and back, in a LES spot a brisk walk south of their store (a new branch is coming in Hudson Yards!).  Well worth the walk and I'm looking forward to a return visit for that sable.

Before trekking on down here, you should know that about 80% of the menu items contain some kind of fish on them. Great for me, but my partner didn't feel great about his options. Luckily we found things to order we'd both enjoy... I had the eggs benny, which came with smoked salmon, poached egg and dreamy hollandaise on the perfect piece of challah bread. I thoroughly enjoyed each bite. My partner ordered the Latkes with apple sauce and it was the the light breakfast he was looking for. Somethings to know about the space, its bright and cute, but small... don't come here with a big party unless you're willing to wait 45-60 minutes. Can't wait to come back and try a few more things.

The cafe is the place to go. My dad and I went on a Friday at about 9:00 am and it was packed. People were there with their suitcases. We had to wait a little bit, but ended up getting two seats the bar top, which was cute. The inside of the cafe has great theming and decoration. Concord Grape Soda ($8) The drinks are pricey because they aren't can sodas, they are freshly made in the cafe. This one has jasmine, timut pepper, and lemon and obviously concord grapes. Their sodas are delicious and you have to be careful not to suck it down too quick! The Classic Board ($22) Nova smoked salmon, cream cheese, your choice of bagel, bialy, rye, or pumpernickel. I love this, it is simple, but delicious and hits every time. It is also very instagrammable the way they plate it. Overall really solid food, fun place to take people from out of town.

Visited Russ and Daughters after watching Somebody Feed Phil Got the egg cream, lox benedict, potato latkes with applesauce and sour cream, rugelach, and chocolate babka french toast. My favorite was the babka french toast (delicious!) followed by the latkes. The rest of the items I thought were ok. Be prepared to put your name down and wait a good 45 minutes just fyi!
This place is really tasty my only criticism is to please add salt and pepper shakers on the table!

We came around 8:30AM and there was no wait. The service was great and our food came out within 10 minutes! The classic salmon board was really good and a must try if you come here! I didn't think I would like it but the smoked salmon/onion/tomato combo was perfect. I really liked being able to put together my bagel too. The green onion cream cheese spread made the bagel even better. I'd also recommend asking for pickled onions to add to your board. I did not enjoy the blintzes due to the cheese texture but my friends liked it. IG: tiffsfoodreview

Russ & Daughters Cafe was the first stop on my wife's birthday extravaganza. We'd been to the OG Russ & Daughter's shop. Good stuff but a lot of hype for bagels, spreads, and fish. I'm quite spoiled with having some great bagel and fish spots nearby, so treking out to the Soho?, Noho?, HoHo? area from Brooklyn or Queens is a big commitment. When we walked in, immediately realized that it was going to be a great experience. Bar upfront with a limited but mindful selection of alcohol. They had Kings County, Blanton's, and Michter's all at reasonable prices. I opted for a spiked egg cream before following my heart to a pour of Kings County bourbon. Service at the bar was quick and attentive. Menu was super intriguing with sections dedicated to herring, caviar, smoked salmon, and Jewish classics. We ended up sharing a daily special - the potato "totkes" - , the white fish chowder, and the babka French toast. Totkes were great. Super crispy and came with a delicious Bloody Mary creme frachie. The smoked white fish chowder was creamy and savory. Tons of veggies and super hearty. Babka French toast is a dessert lover's treat for a meal. Two gender neutral restrooms which were handicap accessible. One had a changing table. We were able to walk in on a weekday but I can imagine needing to get here earlier on the weekends.

Life is great when the plan you had before does not work out, but when Plan B works out better than you ever imagined, better than the original plan you had. This is what happened, and I guess it would be appropriate to say it is a Chanukah miracle. My original plan for lunch today was to go to Katz's Deli for lunch. When I saw the line outside was basically wrapping around the block, I abandoned my plan and decided to go to Russ & Daughters Cafe instead. I have been to the flagship store and know the food is good, but had never been to the cafe for lunch, as I never had the opportunity, and thinking it would just be alright. It is more than alright, it is a treat. A beautiful experience transposed onto a bowl, a board, and a plate. Just be willing to pay up because this will not be cheap. For me at least, since I decided to ante up and go for several things. For starters, the hostess sat me at the counter. No loss. It was a 45 minute wait for the seat as it gets fairly busy for lunch. I can certainly do that. As for the food... yeah buckle up buddy boy. Matzo ball soup: A hearty blend of one golf-sized matzo ball, chicken, some carrots, and a bit of celery. It works beautifully. The presentation is a bit poor because the broth overflow onto the plate it is served with below, but the matzo ball is tasty. This one does it right. However, give me noodles with it and you have a five star appetizer. Score: 4/5 stars Cream Soda: Starts out strong, but quickly fizzles out. Save your money, unless you like quick and easy drinks. Score: 3.5/5 stars Potato latkes: Jewish potato pancakes cooked to maximum effort. Three solid sized bad boys served with your choice of either applesauce and sour cream or cream cheese and caviar. I opted for the former and it was delicious. My Jewish origins were speaking to me as I was eating this, but only in a whisper. Unfortunately I could not eat the last one because it is a dense treat. That being said, I highly recommend these. Score: 4.5/5 stars Shtetl: I was torn between the Classic and this, so I asked my server at the bar. Since I told her I had tried their lox and knew it was good, she directed me to the Shtetl: It is excellent. The goat cream cheese marries well with the sablefish, which almost tastes like whitefish without the mashy mix. The everything bagel is perfectly toasted and perfectly coated with garlic, poppyseeds, and sesame seeds. Even the goat cream cheese is terrific. I could have eaten this alone just out of the ramekin, but restrained myself from doing so. It is also served with tomatoes, onions, and capers, but I am simple. No need for these! Reminder my Jewish origins whispering to me? They were speaking pretty loudly after this one. Score: 5/5 stars Now, for the topper... Egg cream: This is as New York as it gets. However, I learned too quickly that you have to drink this fast as the frothy top disappears, and then you are left with a borderline nasty mixture of milk, seltzer, and chocolate syrup. Still solid way to end any meal, but drink up! Score: 4/5 stars ***Bonus*** During Chanukah, Russ and Daughters sells a limited time offer of three jelly donuts that they make, as jelly donuts are an iconic food during Chanukah. One that is of the black and white cookie style, one that is an original jelly donut with strawberry jam, and one that looks and tastes like a strawberry rugelach that also has strawberry jam. All three are fabulous and you will wish they served these year round. The fact the servers everywhere were hyping this up is telling you to get this either as you walk out the door, or as a sweet treat to wrap up a flawless lunch. Score: 5/5 stars ---- A Lower East Side without Russ & Daughter's and Katz's is unfathomable. It still transplants you to a time when these establishments dominated Delancey St and W Houston St. Thankfully, if all continues to go well, they will continue to be here, and continue to remind customers, now and in the future, what made this area so special and unique at the turn of the century. Life is a funny thing, is it not?
If you do not like fish do not go here! $123 for two salads, a dessert, and two cocktails. Uptown feel inside but still cozy. Food is meh.

The cafe is a full-service version of the famed shop a few blocks away. The first time I visited, it was during  a pandemic flare and they were doing takeout. I ordered as-is bagels and fish to go, along with a toasted pumpernickel bagel with butter and lox and pumpernickel bread. It was easy to order online and pickup. And everything was delicious. I went back a year later for a sit down breakfast. A short line formed before opening and the cafe filled quickly. It's got an old-school diner feel. I ordered the bagel board with a pumpernickel bagel (shocking). It was great. The staff is super friendly and I look forward to returning.

I ordered bagels, sable, pumpernickel loaf, and a pumpernickel bagel with butter and lox. I ordered online early that morning and it was ready right on time, perfectly timed for my dad to pick me up nearby and eat my bagels. Everything was excellent. Sable is my absolute favorite, and near impossible to find where I live. Theirs is perfectly succulent, and buttery. Bagel was delicious and obviously, the lox is super high quality. I love pumpernickel, hence the bagel and the loaf, and theirs is so flavorful and better than most. Take home bagels were good even a few days later. You wait outside, tell the staff member your name, and they come out with your order. It's really easy and the staff is friendly. I can't wait to return to Russ & Daughters.

Delicious salmon lox and great service! The salmon tasted very aromatic and the bagels tasted fresh. I highly recommend getting them toasted. The service was great. The check comes with a Russ & Daughters postcard, and when I took a picture of it, another waiter noticed and quickly gave us a couple more postcards. I also said the word "dessert" and my table's waiter immediately started pointing out the dessert options.
The bagels are amazing. Everything else, not so much.  The matzah balls fall apart while heating, the rugelach isn't fresh as it should be! Just stick to the bagels and you'll be fine.

Stopped in for a late morning bite. They don't take reservations, while it was busy my party of 2 was seated within 15 minutes. Started with the potato latkes with apple sauce and sour cream. Best latkes I've ever had. Ordered and shared the classic - smoked salmon with tomato onion capers cream cheese and choice of bagel - and the yum kippered - baked same otherwise the same as the classic. Both were amazing. Also ordered the pickle platter which was amazing. Finished with the bread pudding which was warm and delicious. Fun restaurant with great food and friendly staff. Has a bit of classic NYC LES deli feel to it. Also conveniently can stop at the Russ and daughters deli right near by.

We arrived a few minutes before opening on the Friday after Turkey Day. Almost no line and the place never got crowded (a very off day). Service is always good and the selections are huge. We had the omelette with veggies and "Lower Sunny Side" and 2 freshly brewed decafs. A nice and tasty breakfast. Pete Wells was spot on this time. Recommended! Damages with tip for 2 was $70 - hey this is NYC!

We happened to be in town the weekend after they reopened after a 2-year COVID closure. We went early - arriving 10 minutes before they opened - expecting a line - but were FIRST (a first for us). A small line formed soon but surprisingly the cafe only got about half full. Guess the word is not yet out that they are back. I expect that many of the staff were new (in fact our server said he just started) but things are running well. We had coffees and juices and the "Lower Sunny Side" and "Lox, eggs, and onions". Both entrees at $22 each. All swell and the quality and authenticity that you expect from R&D. Damages with tip was $75. Food       5/5 Service   4/5 Value     3/5 (hey this is NYC!) Cleanliness  5/5 Noise     5/5 (a quiet crowd) Decor     5/5 Go early and enjoy!

This is a real treat and HIGHLY recommended. We had usually used their other store for takeout. We got one of the last tables (845 AM) before the crowds and wait began. Service was excellent and who could not like the food. The only downside vs. takeout from their other store is that there are only a few salmon types available (vs. a zillion). Coffees (with free and frequent refills!). Entrees were various bagels with salmon, "Lower Sunny Side", and granola. You will not be disappointed. Food            5/5 Service        5/5 Value           4/5 Cleanliness  5/5 Noise           4/5 (you can talk) Decor           4/5

This is an excellent spot for amazing and flavorful food! I'd been here before and it was nice to return and enjoy the great offerings. I went for the Classic Board and it did not disappoint - it included a fresh bagel and wonderful smoked salmon with all the accompaniments. Everything tasted great and one can tell that the quality is top-notch. The setting is like a chic diner - it's a wonderful space to be in. We experienced warm and friendly service...the host and server treated us very well and it helped to ensure a memorable experience. This place is very popular, so make sure to plan accordingly; if you arrive at typical brunch times, expect a long wait.
Overhyped and over priced support a local spot. Cheap ingredients could remake everything from Walmart. Bad bad bad. Expect Walmart quality. Just bad ingredients

This restaurant hits all the right notes. We arrived five minutes after opening on a gloomy day and were seated immediately. The nova board was perfection with a fresh, light bagel, tender nova (not salty or fishy), ripe tomatoes and tasty condiments. They offer house still or seltzer water. With the parent company's 100 years plus in the business they have mastered the art of this cuisine.

Levain can do no wrong in my book as I'm a fan of well balanced chocolate chip cookies. I appreciate some crunch and some mushy and measuring chocolate chips with one's soul. Plus their cookies are generous which is perfect for sharing! I tend to like a sprinkle of salt as well and that may be the only thing missing from their cookie selection. I just stick with the classic. The past few times I've been, I've ventured out of chocolate chip cookies and have tried their cakes. The seasonal ginger one is so delightful. I appreciated the spicy kick and it was a big hit with young and old. Sadly, I tried to repurchase recently and was told it was an autumn special. I've tried their banana choc chip cake loaf as well, and love that the banana taste really comes through. Not too sweet. In terms of customer space, this location is teeny with lots of offerings so you often see people hanging out outside waiting for some space to clear to place an order. With two registers, however, everything tends to move quickly. This is a great location for us uptowners!

Yodalis, thank you for being such a loyal fan of our Frederick Douglass Boulevard bakery! We're so glad you've been enjoying both our classic treats and seasonal cakes. Your feedback about our Harlem location is much appreciated! Sincerely, The Levain Team

Wow, wow... and yes, WOW. Levain Bakery is not playing fair in the cookie game. Coming from Miami, where most cookie vendors leans on the side of extra sweet, Levain somehow gives you all that richness without doing the absolute most. It's bold, it's indulgent, but it knows when to hold back. Much respect to their game. I told myself I'd be responsible and got a tin so I could bring them home for the hubbs, because growth and our highly favorable co-dependency. Meanwhile, my friend got hers warmed and handed me a piece of the chocolate chip walnut... and I almost melted, it was just incredible. From there it was downhill, in the best way. I ordered pretty much everything. After arriving home we enjoyed them all together, but the dark chocolate chocolate chip and that caramel coconut? Yeah... those two stood out to me the most. Now the real question. When are they coming to South Florida? Because I'm not trying to catch flights every time I need this level of happiness.

Shikira, thank you for bringing your husband's cookies all the way back to Miami and for sharing such a thoughtful review of your visit to our Frederick Douglass Blvd bakery! We're thrilled you got to sample so many varieties, especially the dark chocolate chocolate chip and caramel coconut. Hope to see you soon! Warmly, The Levain Team

Absolutely amazing cookies. We had a caramel coconut chocolate chip and it was the perfect balance of salty and sweet. It also felt especially soft. Also had the seasonal lemon cookie and it was the perfect amount of lemon.  It's a small store front but they still had the full selection. Also love the little levain postcards

Zoe, we're thrilled you enjoyed both treats at our Frederick Douglass Blvd bakery! That combination of flavors really hits the spot, and we're so glad the seasonal option was a winner too. Thanks for noticing those postcards - they're a fun little touch we love sharing! Warmly, The Levain Team

The fall spiced chocolate chunk was very good. The chocolate and molasses were perfect together!!! As always the walnut chocolate chip and the double chocolate chip were perfect. The double chocolate chip cookie was still a bit warm. The peanut butter chocolate cookie was certainly a miss. It was very dry. I think of all the times I've been to levain, this is the first time I've been disappointed by one of the cookies.
Kristina, we appreciate your feedback on the peanut butter chocolate cookie. Thank you for visiting our Frederick Douglass Blvd bakery - we hope to have you back soon! - The Levain Team

World renowned bakery beginning back in the 90's recognized by The New Yorker and New York Times for their cookies! And cookies is what we got! Oatmeal Raisin, Lemon, Chocolate Chip Walnut, and a Caramel Coconut! In addition, one Blueberry Muffin. All of the cookies are moist but crunchy and they are HUGE! Absolutely delicious Quiet shop with small dine in, mostly takeout. Great friendly staff.

Norman, we're thrilled you enjoyed your recent visit to our Harlem bakery! It's wonderful to hear you appreciated the warm hospitality of our team members. We look forward to welcoming you back soon. Warmly, The Levain Team

Still one of the best cookies in the world! Im gonna keep this short and sweet. Cookies are great. Service is great. Nice that they added a lil table and chair out front so you could enjoy what ever you purchased on site. Prices are still decent, if you haven't been, what are you waiting for. To many location in this city for you not to indulge. Two thumbs up, Happy Yelping!

Bernice, thanks for your kind words and support! We're overjoyed you continue to enjoy our fresh-baked cookies. Having an inviting space to savor our treats is important to us, and we appreciate your feedback. Hope to welcome you back soon! Warmly, The Levain Team

The best warm chocolate walnut chunky cookie I ever had. The girl was nice enough to give it to me fresh out of the oven, it will go so well with some vanilla ice cream in the  summer season or anytime. It was quite small inside, mostly all bakery. I would try some of the other goodies on my next visit, but this one was for the cookie. A very darn good cookie. If im not up for baking myself, this is the place to make my order.

First time having levain and it was so delicious!! Tried the caramel coconut chocolate chip - highly recommend!!! The coconut was not overpowering This was ordered via delivery and it was still warm when it got here

Hi Gloria, we're thrilled to hear that your first Levain experience was a hit! The caramel coconut chocolate chip is indeed a delightful choice, and we're glad you enjoyed the balance of flavors. It's fantastic to know that your delivery arrived warm and ready to enjoy. Thanks for recommending us, and we hope to bring more deliciousness to your doorstep soon! - The Levain Team
